AustralianElectricityMarkets.FCAS_INACTIVE_LIMIT_MW Constant
julia
FCAS_INACTIVE_LIMIT_MW

Right-hand side, in MW, of an FCAS row at an interval where it does not apply (an offer not enabled under AEMO FCAS Model in NEMDE §5, or a ramping row without a ramp rate or InitialMW): +FCAS_INACTIVE_LIMIT_MW for a <= row and -FCAS_INACTIVE_LIMIT_MW for a >= row. AustralianElectricityMarkets.NEM_OBSERVED_SERIES Constant
julia
NEM_OBSERVED_SERIES

Names of the per-device SingleTimeSeries that set_unit_conditions! attaches for a unit's NEMObservedState, in AEMO's natural units: initial_mw (INITIALMW, MW), dispatch_mode (DISPATCHMODE of the previous interval) and dispatch_mode_time (DISPATCHMODETIME of the previous interval, minutes).

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.NEM_SERIES Constant
julia
NEM_SERIES

Names of the per-device SingleTimeSeries the setters attach, by field:

  • ramp_up_rate, ramp_down_rate: the dispatch ramp rates the formulation reads, system-base per-unit per minute, derived by the NEMDE input stage from the telemetry ramp limits.

  • max_active_power: the device's upper dispatch limit, a multiplier of its max_active_power.

  • loss_demand_coefficient: an interchange's demand term of its loss factor.

The unit condition series are named by NEM_TELEMETRY_SERIES and NEM_OBSERVED_SERIES, and held by the device's NEMTelemetry and NEMObservedState.

Offer-side series are named by energy_offer_series_name and fcas_series_name.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.NEM_STATE_INPUT_SERIES Constant
julia
NEM_STATE_INPUT_SERIES

Names of the per-device SingleTimeSeries that the NEMDE input stage derives from a unit's NEMObservedState and fixed loading, read by the dispatch formulation at each interval:

  • initial_mw: the output at the start of each interval, MW, zero at an interval the build does not observe.

  • fixed_load: the fixed-loading target in system-base per-unit, net injection.

  • fixed_load_invoked: 1 at the intervals a fixed loading applies, 0 elsewhere.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.NEM_TELEMETRY_SERIES Constant
julia
NEM_TELEMETRY_SERIES

Names of the per-device SingleTimeSeries that set_unit_conditions! attaches for a unit's NEMTelemetry, in AEMO's natural units, as DISPATCHLOAD publishes them:

  • agc_status: AGCSTATUS, 0 or 1, NaN at an interval with no row.

  • uigf: UIGF, MW, semi-scheduled units only.

  • ramp_up_limit, ramp_down_limit: RAMPUPRATE, RAMPDOWNRATE, MW/h.

  • raise_reg_enablement, lower_reg_enablement: the (min, max) MW enablement of each service.

  • raise_reg_max_avail, lower_reg_max_avail: the regulation maximum availability, MW.

AEMO's DIRECTION of a bid: GEN (generation), LOAD (consumption) or BIDIRECTIONAL, an FCAS bid that a storage device offers on both sides. A BIDIRECTIONAL FCAS bid is modelled on the generation side.

The state-independent inputs of one device's state-dependent NEMDE inputs over the System's range, read once and prepared per family on first use, so that a closed-loop step evaluates only the state-dependent rules. Build with closed_loop_inputs and evaluate with closed_loop_input.

Abstract supertype for one linear term on a GenericConstraint's LHS. Concrete subtypes hold names, not live component references — see GenericConstraint for why. Factors are in natural MW, matching AEMO's own FACTOR columns; not per-unitized by BASE_POWER.

julia
EnergyTieBreak(; name, available = true, ext = Dict{String, Any}(), internal = InfrastructureSystemsInternal())

The anchor of the energy tie-break rows: the add_service! join between the tie-break and the units whose price-tied energy bands it dispatches pro rata. Carries no time series of its own; each unit's band scales live on the unit.

Fields

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.FCASTrapezium Type

AEMO FCAS trapezium parameters for one device's offer into one FCAS market. Zero below enablement_min, ramping to max_avail at low_breakpoint, flat until high_breakpoint, ramping back to zero at enablement_max (AEMO, FCAS Model in NEMDE, §2). All MW/MW-per-minute fields are as the Simulations package's FCAS trapezium readers return them: MW under NATURAL_UNITS, per-unit of the system base under SYSTEM_BASE.

A fast-start unit's dispatch mode at the end of an interval, from fast_start_end_state.

Fields

AustralianElectricityMarkets.FastStartEnvelope Type
julia
FastStartEnvelope(lower, upper, ramp, ramp_base, ramp_minutes)

The bounds a fast-start unit's energy target takes in NEMDE's dispatch run, from fast_start_envelope, on the offer side's axis, and the treatment of its energy ramp rows.

Fields

  • lower: the profile's lower bound on the target, MW.

  • upper: the profile's upper bound on the target, MW, Inf where the profile sets none.

  • ramp: :none when the unit has no energy ramp rows, :from_minimum_load when its ramp-up row starts at ramp_base and runs for ramp_minutes (its ramp-down row is unchanged), :standard when both rows are the unit's usual rows about its initial output.

  • ramp_base: the minimum loading for :from_minimum_load, MW, NaN otherwise.

  • ramp_minutes: the time since the end of mode 2 for :from_minimum_load, minutes, NaN otherwise.

FastStartUnitInputs

The fast-start inputs of one unit at one interval, from fast_start_unit_inputs, in natural units.

Fields

  • fast_start: whether the offer's profile makes the unit fast-start in the interval (is_fast_start).

  • side: the OfferSide of the energy bid carrying the profile; the profile applies to the target on that side's axis (consumption for a load).

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.GenericConstraint Type

A NEM generic constraint, LHS <sense> RHS — the mechanism AEMO uses for both network limits and FCAS requirements. Attached to its contributing devices as a PSY.Service.

Fields

  • name: identifier — GENCONID@EFFECTIVEDATE#VERSIONNO for an AEMO-sourced constraint.

  • available: whether it is enforced.

  • sense: LE, GE or EQ, from GENCONDATA.CONSTRAINTTYPE.

  • rhs: GENCONDATA.CONSTRAINTVALUE in MW as published, or a key of the per-interval right-hand side series in MW; read it with get_rhs.

  • invoked: whether the constraint is enforced, or a key of the per-interval invoked series; read it with get_invoked.

  • constraint_weight: GENCONDATA.GENERICCONSTRAINTWEIGHT verbatim; 1.0 for a constraint whose source is "built-in", which has no GENCONDATA row.

  • description: human-readable, defaults to "".

  • gencon_id: GENCONDATA.GENCONID without the version suffix; defaults to the part of name before @.

  • limit_type: GENCONDATA.LIMITTYPE, or nothing if absent.

  • source: GENCONDATA.SOURCE, or nothing if absent.

  • effective_date: GENCONDATA.EFFECTIVEDATE, or nothing if absent.

  • version_no: GENCONDATA.VERSIONNO, or nothing if absent.

  • terms: the LHS algebra, from the SPD* tables.

  • fcas_requirements: the (region, service) prices this constraint governs.

  • ext: free-form annotations; a NEMDE build leaves it empty.

  • internal: InfrastructureSystems bookkeeping.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.InterconnectorKindModule.InterconnectorKind Type
julia
InterconnectorKind

AEMO's INTERCONNECTORCONSTRAINT.ICTYPE: REGULATED for an interconnector with no offers, MNSP for one whose flow AEMO dispatches through two directional offers.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.InterconnectorLossModel Type
julia
InterconnectorLossModel

One interconnector's NEMDE loss model, resolved to a single EFFECTIVEDATE/VERSIONNO.

NEMDE treats interconnector losses as a quadratic in flow whose linear coefficient shifts with regional demand: the loss factor at flow f is

julia
lf(f) = loss_constant + loss_flow_coefficient * f + Σ_{r∈regions} demand_coefficients[r] * demand[r]

and the losses themselves are the integral of lf(f) - 1 over [0, f] — see interconnector_losses. MWBREAKPOINT (LOSSMODEL) supplies the breakpoints NEMDE linearises that quadratic on, reproduced by loss_segments.

Fields

  • interconnector: INTERCONNECTORID.

  • from_region/to_region: REGIONFROM/REGIONTO; flow is positive from → to.

  • from_region_loss_share: fraction of losses attributed to from_region.

  • loss_constant: LOSSCONSTANT.

  • loss_flow_coefficient: LOSSFLOWCOEFFICIENT, natural-units MW unless the model has been per-unitized (see attach_interconnector_losses!).

  • demand_coefficients: REGIONID => DEMANDCOEFFICIENT, same units convention as loss_flow_coefficient.

  • breakpoints: MWBREAKPOINT values, ascending, same units convention as loss_flow_coefficient.

  • internal: InfrastructureSystems bookkeeping.

A model returned by interconnector_loss_models carries natural-units MW throughout; one attached to a System by attach_interconnector_losses! is per-unit of that System's base power instead. loss_factor/interconnector_losses/ loss_segments are unit-agnostic - flow/demand must be passed in whichever convention model itself uses.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.InterconnectorTerm Type

A FACTOR * <interconnector flow> term, from SPDINTERCONNECTORCONSTRAINT.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.MNSPDirectionModule.MNSPDirection Type
julia
MNSPDirection

The direction of one MNSP bid: FORWARD for flow from the interchange's from_area to its to_area, REVERSE for the opposite flow.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.NEMBuildReport Type
julia
NEMBuildReport(; skipped_constraints = Dict{String, Any}[], missing_constraint_intervals = DateTime[],
    defaulted_constraint_weights = String[], dropped_terms = Dict{String, Any}[],
    unavailable_constraints = Dict{String, Any}[])

What nem_system left out of, or defaulted in, the constraints it built into a System, and which built constraints the NEMDE inputs made unavailable.

Fields

  • skipped_constraints: one row per invoked constraint version that was not built, with constraint, reason and missing (the unresolved keys).

  • missing_constraint_intervals: the dispatch intervals with no invoked constraint.

  • defaulted_constraint_weights: the versioned names built with the default constraint_weight.

  • dropped_terms: one row per unit term dropped from a built constraint, with constraint, kind, key, bid_type, factor and registered (the unit is registered at some interval of the build range).

  • unavailable_constraints: one row per built constraint set unavailable by the NEMDE inputs, with constraint and reason ("never_invoked" or "no_available_device").

    normal_status = nothing, energy_limit = nothing, band_prices = nothing)

One side of a unit's energy offer as AEMO bid it: each field is a static value or a key of the time series that holds it on the unit, or nothing where AEMO publishes no value.

Fields

  • roc_up, roc_down: ROCUP and ROCDOWN, MW/min.

  • fixed_load: FIXEDLOAD, MW, with NaN at the intervals where AEMO publishes NULL, or nothing where every interval's value is NULL or zero.

  • minimum_load: MINIMUMLOAD, MW.

  • fast_start_profile: T1 to T4, as a FastStartProfile, in minutes.

  • daily_energy_constraint: DAILYENERGYCONSTRAINT, MWh.

  • normal_status: NORMALSTATUS, true for ON.

  • energy_limit: ENERGYLIMIT, MWh.

  • band_prices: the ten band prices of the trading day in $/MWh at the reference node, padded with 0.0, or nothing until the NEMDE inputs are written.

AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_constraint_definitions Function
julia
read_constraint_definitions(db, gencon_versions)

gencon_versions has distinct (GENCONID, GENCONID_EFFECTIVEDATE, GENCONID_VERSIONNO) rows (see read_invoked_constraints). Joins each to its exact GENCONDATA version: CONSTRAINTTYPE, GENERICCONSTRAINTWEIGHT, CONSTRAINTVALUE, plus DESCRIPTION/LIMITTYPE/SOURCE. A GENCONID absent from the result has no GENCONDATA row for that exact version — usually because the defining archive month isn't cached (see read_fcas_requirements) — callers must treat that as "no definition available". Throws an ArgumentError on an empty gencon_versions: nothing was invoked over the range, which means DISPATCHCONSTRAINT was never cached for it.

AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_demand Function
julia
read_demand(db; resolution::Dates.Period=Dates.Minute(5), intervention::Integer=0)
read_demand(db, date_range; resolution::Dates.Period=Dates.Minute(5), intervention::Integer=0)

Read regional demand and aggregate it at resolution. When date_range is provided, read only the raw intervals contributing to aggregate timestamps in [first(date_range), last(date_range)).

Arguments

  • db: The database connection.

  • date_range: Optional range of aggregate timestamps, with an inclusive start and exclusive end.

  • resolution::Dates.Period: The time resolution to which timestamps are rounded up. Defaults to 5 minutes.

  • intervention::Integer: 0 for the pricing run. 1 for the physical run where the interval has one, else the pricing run. Each of DISPATCHREGIONSUM and DISPATCHLOAD decides its run per interval; AEMO publishes both runs for an intervention interval, so region sums and unit loads come from the same run. Ignored where the cached partitions predate the INTERVENTION column.

Returns

A DataFrame with regional demand, aggregated by the specified resolution. LOSSDEMAND is INITIALSUPPLY + DEMANDFORECAST plus the initial charging load of the region's BIDIRECTIONAL units (DISPATCHLOAD.INITIALMW where negative), with unit type and region resolved as of the interval.

Example

julia
db = aem_connect()
demand_df = read_demand(db; resolution=Dates.Hour(1))
println(demand_df)
source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_dispatch_limits Function
julia
read_dispatch_limits(db, date_range; intervention = 0, resolution = Minute(5))

Reads per-unit dispatch limits from DISPATCHLOAD: INITIALMW, RAMPUPRATE, RAMPDOWNRATE and AVAILABILITY, the ramp rates and dispatch envelope NEMDE applied for each 5-minute interval. AVAILABILITY is the MAXAVAIL bid availability of a scheduled unit, or the lower of MAXAVAIL and UIGF for a semi-scheduled unit.

With a resolution coarser than five minutes, the intervals are ceiled onto it and each bucket keeps the INITIALMW at its first interval (the metered MW at the start of the period) and the minimum of each ramp rate and AVAILABILITY across its intervals.

Warning

Coarse buckets aggregate the available rows without checking five-minute coverage. An incomplete bucket can shift INITIALMW away from the period start and omit more restrictive ramp rates or availability limits. Ensure the cache covers every five-minute interval.

Arguments

  • db: an AEMDB connection.

  • date_range: the dispatch intervals to read (half-open: start <= t < stop).

  • intervention: 0 for the pricing run. 1 for the physical run where the interval has one, else the pricing run.

  • resolution: the Dates.Period to aggregate onto. Defaults to 5 minutes.

Returns

A DataFrame with SETTLEMENTDATE, DUID, INITIALMW, RAMPUPRATE, RAMPDOWNRATE, AVAILABILITY. Throws an ArgumentError when DISPATCHLOAD is not cached or lacks a column.

Reads the latest energy period offers from BIDPEROFFER_D: one row per (SETTLEMENTDATE, INTERVAL_DATETIME, DUID, DIRECTION) with MAXAVAIL and the BANDAVAIL columns. With a resolution, INTERVAL_DATETIME is ceiled onto it and each bucket keeps the maximum of every quantity.

Arguments

  • date_range: the intervals to read (half-open: start <= INTERVAL_DATETIME < stop).

  • resolution: a Dates.Period to aggregate onto, or nothing for the raw intervals.

Returns

AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_fcas_bids Function
julia
read_fcas_bids(db, date_range, bid_type::BidType; resolution = nothing)
read_fcas_bids(db, date_range, bid_types::AbstractVector{BidType}; resolution = nothing)

Like read_bids, but for an AEMO FCAS bid_type (e.g. BidType.RAISE6SEC, BidType.RAISEREG — see FCAS_BID_TYPES). Reuses _massage_bids for the 10-band offer (same columns as the energy bid path), and additionally reads the AEMO FCAS trapezium columns from BIDPEROFFER_D (ENABLEMENTMIN/MAX, LOWBREAKPOINT, HIGHBREAKPOINT, ROCUP, ROCDOWN — already present in that table, just never selected by the energy-only bid path).

With a vector of bid_types the tables are read once for all of them and the result carries an extra BIDTYPE column (BidType).

With a resolution above five minutes, each bucket's trapezium comes from the native row at the bucket's last interval, not from an average over the bucket.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_fcas_dispatch Function
julia
read_fcas_dispatch(db, date_range; intervention = 0)

Reads per-interval, per-unit FCAS dispatch outcomes from DISPATCHLOAD, long-format: one row per (SETTLEMENTDATE, DUID, BIDTYPE::BidType, TARGET, ACTUALAVAILABILITY), plus the unit's energy context columns INITIALMW, TOTALCLEARED, AVAILABILITY, AGCSTATUS. This is the cleared counterpart to read_fcas_bids's offered trapezium - comparing TARGET/ACTUALAVAILABILITY against the offer's trapezium shows how much of what a unit offered was actually deliverable at its dispatched energy level (see AustralianElectricityMarkets.FCASTrapezium).

ACTUALAVAILABILITY is missing for the two regulation markets (RAISEREG/LOWERREG) - AEMO does not publish a trapezium-adjusted availability for regulation, only the raw offer availability (RAISEREGAVAILABILITY/LOWERREGAVAILABILITY).

intervention selects the dispatch run: 0 for the pricing run. 1 for the physical run where the interval has one, else the pricing run. A table without an INTERVENTION column is read unfiltered.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_fcas_prices Function
julia
read_fcas_prices(db, date_range; intervention = 0)

Reads per-interval, per-region FCAS clearing prices from DISPATCHPRICE, long-format: one row per (SETTLEMENTDATE, REGIONID, BIDTYPE::BidType) with RRP, ROP, APCFLAG. Summing read_fcas_requirements's MARGINALVALUE per (REGIONID, BIDTYPE) reproduces ROP for that interval (not RRP, which may additionally be capped).

Arguments

  • db: an AEMDB connection.

  • date_range: the dispatch intervals to read (half-open: start <= t < stop).

  • intervention: 0 for the pricing run. 1 for the physical run where the interval has one, else the pricing run.

Returns

A DataFrame with SETTLEMENTDATE, REGIONID, RRP, ROP, APCFLAG and BIDTYPE. Markets without cached price columns are absent; APCFLAG is missing where its column is not cached.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_fcas_requirements Function
julia
read_fcas_requirements(db, date_range; intervention = 0)

Reads per-interval, per-region FCAS requirement constraints actually enforced in dispatch, long-format: one row per (SETTLEMENTDATE, REGIONID, BIDTYPE::BidType, GENCONID).

AEMO stopped populating the RESERVE table (and DISPATCHREGIONSUM's *REQ columns) in Dec 2003 - confirmed directly, both URL patterns 404 for every month tried. The modern mechanism is generic-constraint-based: DISPATCH_FCAS_REQ maps each (region, service, interval) to the GENCONID of the generic constraint governing it (a region/service can be governed by more than one constraint at once - e.g. a regulation market's target also appears on a contingency constraint's LHS - so this is joined, not aggregated, to one row per governing constraint).

Each row is a linear constraint LHS CONSTRAINTTYPE REQUIREMENT (CONSTRAINTTYPE is <=/>=/=), not a standalone MW quantity - REQUIREMENT (DISPATCHCONSTRAINT.RHS) is only meaningful together with LHS (DISPATCHCONSTRAINT.LHS, the FCAS-and-related dispatch terms NEMDE actually summed) and CONSTRAINTTYPE. Two regimes are common in practice:

  • Disarmed: AEMO switches an inapplicable constraint variant off by offsetting its REQUIREMENT by a large negative multiple of 10,000 so it can never bind regardless of LHS - a REQUIREMENT far below any plausible FCAS quantity (in the thousands or tens of thousands negative) is this, not a literal deficit. MARGINALVALUE is always 0.0 for these rows.

  • Armed: REQUIREMENT is the real bound. It can still be negative here - the same region/service is often governed by more than one constraint variant (e.g. one that nets FCAS against an interconnector flow term on LHS), and only one variant is armed at a time. Compare LHS to REQUIREMENT under CONSTRAINTTYPE to see whether the constraint is satisfied or violated; MARGINALVALUE != 0.0 confirms it is binding.

MARGINALVALUE is the constraint's shadow price, and summing it per (REGIONID, BIDTYPE) reproduces the regional FCAS price (see read_fcas_prices). GENCONDATA is joined in only for its human-readable DESCRIPTION/CONSTRAINTTYPE - GENCONDATA is a change-only table (a constraint version appears only in the archive month it was published), so a missing DESCRIPTION/CONSTRAINTTYPE usually means the defining archive month isn't in the local cache, not that AEMO never published one.

intervention selects the dispatch run: 0 for the pricing run. 1 for the physical run where the interval has one, else the pricing run.

Throws an ArgumentError when neither DISPATCH_FCAS_REQ nor DISPATCH_FCAS_REQ_CONSTRAINT is cached.

AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_loss_factors Function

read_loss_factors(db; as_of = nothing, through = nothing) -> DataFrame

Reads each unit's connection-point loss factors from DUDETAILSUMMARY: the row with START_DATE <= as_of < END_DATE in the latest archive.

Arguments

  • through: with as_of, resolves the factors over the window [as_of, through] instead: each unit's earliest row registered in it, the row read_units keeps with the same through. Warns if a unit's factors differ between its rows in the window, since the result holds one factor per unit.

Returns

AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_mnsp_offers Function
julia
read_mnsp_offers(db, date_range)

Reads the MNSP link offers NEMDE applied in each dispatch interval of date_range.

Each interval's offer is the one named by DISPATCH_MNSPBIDTRK (dispatch run 1), joined to its MNSP_DAYOFFER price bands and its MNSP_BIDOFFERPERIOD availability for that interval's five-minute period of the trading day. The tables cover trading days from the start of five-minute settlement (1 October 2021); earlier intervals are not supported.

Arguments

  • db: The database connection.

  • date_range: Interval-ending timestamps; intervals t with first(date_range) <= t < last(date_range) are returned.

Returns

A DataFrame with one row per (INTERVAL_DATETIME, LINKID): PARTICIPANTID, MAXAVAIL, FIXEDLOAD (missing when no fixed load), RAMPUPRATE, BANDAVAIL1-BANDAVAIL10 and PRICEBAND1-PRICEBAND10.

Example

julia
db = aem_connect()
offers = read_mnsp_offers(db, DateTime(2026, 6, 15, 12):Minute(5):DateTime(2026, 6, 15, 13))

AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_offers Function
julia
read_offers(db, date_range; markets = NEM_MARKETS) -> DataFrame

Reads the latest energy and FCAS offers of markets in one query: BIDPEROFFER_D period offers joined to their BIDDAYOFFER_D price bands, at native resolution. Each row is one (SETTLEMENTDATE, INTERVAL_DATETIME, DUID, DIRECTION, BIDTYPE) with first(date_range) <= INTERVAL_DATETIME < last(date_range). When BIDDAYOFFER is cached, the MINIMUMLOAD and T1 to T4 of an energy row come from the daily offer version in force at the interval: the latest BIDDAYOFFER.OFFERDATE at or before the period offer's LASTCHANGED. Rows without such a version, and every row when BIDDAYOFFER is not cached, keep the BIDDAYOFFER_D values.

Arguments

  • db: an AEMDB connection.

  • date_range: the intervals to read (half-open).

  • markets: the BidType values to read, default NEM_MARKETS.

Returns

A DataFrame with SETTLEMENTDATE, INTERVAL_DATETIME, DUID, DIRECTION, BIDTYPE (BidType), PRICEBANDARRAY, BANDAVAILARRAY, MAXAVAIL, MINIMUMLOAD, DAILYENERGYCONSTRAINT, T1, T2, T3, T4, NORMALSTATUS, FIXEDLOAD, ROCUP, ROCDOWN, ENERGYLIMIT, ENABLEMENTMIN, LOWBREAKPOINT, HIGHBREAKPOINT and ENABLEMENTMAX. Throws an ArgumentError naming any of these columns absent from the cached tables, and when a unit's period offers have no price bands.

RRP is the settlement price and ROP the price before scaling, capping or VoLL override; they differ exactly when APCFLAG != 0 (an administered price cap event). See read_fcas_prices for the FCAS markets.

Arguments

  • date_range: the dispatch intervals to read (half-open: start <= t < stop).

  • intervention: 0 for the pricing run. 1 for the physical run where the interval has one, else the pricing run.

Returns

A DataFrame with SETTLEMENTDATE, REGIONID, RRP, ROP and APCFLAG (missing for cached partitions without the column).

read_published_interval(db, settlement_date; intervention = 0)
read_published_interval(db, steps::StepRange{DateTime}; intervention = 0)

Reads AEMO's published outcome for one dispatch interval, or for every interval of steps in one query per table.

  • steps: the SETTLEMENTDATEs of consecutive intervals, stepping by 5 minutes.

For steps, every table has a leading SETTLEMENTDATE column, and the rows at each interval are those of the single-interval method.

AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_uigf Function
julia
read_uigf(db, date_range; resolution = Minute(5), intervention = 0)

Reads the per-unit Unconstrained Intermittent Generation Forecast (DISPATCHLOAD.UIGF), the upper limit NEMDE applies to each semi-scheduled unit in each dispatch interval. Only DUIDs that DUDETAILSUMMARY lists as SEMI-SCHEDULED at the interval appear. Rows are ceiled onto resolution and averaged within each bucket, as read_demand does.

Arguments

  • db: an AEMDB connection.

  • date_range: the range of interval timestamps to read (half-open: start <= t < stop).

  • resolution: the resolution to aggregate onto. Defaults to 5 minutes.

  • intervention: 0 for the pricing run. 1 for the physical run where the interval has one, else the pricing run.

Returns

A DataFrame with SETTLEMENTDATE, DUID and UIGF (MW). Throws an ArgumentError when DISPATCHLOAD or DUDETAILSUMMARY is not cached, DUDETAILSUMMARY has no SCHEDULE_TYPE, or DISPATCHLOAD has no UIGF column in its cached partitions.

Example

AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_unit_conditions Function
julia
read_unit_conditions(db, date_range; intervention = 0) -> DataFrame

Reads each unit's operating condition from one DISPATCHLOAD read: the metered and dispatch state (INITIALMW, AVAILABILITY, RAMPUPRATE, RAMPDOWNRATE, UIGF, DISPATCHMODE, DISPATCHMODETIME, AGCSTATUS), the regulation enablement limits and the regulation availabilities, for each interval of the half-open date_range. Rates are as published: MW/h, and the ramp rates are the lesser of bid and telemetered rate.

Arguments

  • date_range: the five-minute dispatch intervals to read (half-open: start <= t < stop).

  • intervention: 0 for the pricing run. 1 for the physical run where the interval has one, else the pricing run.

Returns

A DataFrame with SETTLEMENTDATE, DUID, INITIALMW, AVAILABILITY, RAMPUPRATE, RAMPDOWNRATE, UIGF, DISPATCHMODE, DISPATCHMODETIME, AGCSTATUS, RAISEREGENABLEMENTMIN, RAISEREGENABLEMENTMAX, LOWERREGENABLEMENTMIN, LOWERREGENABLEMENTMAX, RAISEREGAVAILABILITY and LOWERREGAVAILABILITY, sorted by DUID and SETTLEMENTDATE. Throws an ArgumentError when DISPATCHLOAD is not cached or a cached partition lacks one of these columns.

AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_units Function
julia
read_units(db; as_of = nothing, through = nothing)

Reads commissioned unit metadata, one row per DUID including scheduled loads. Scheduled loads have no GENUNITS row, so their CO2E_ENERGY_SOURCE is missing. Every row carries the registration span REGISTERED_FROM and REGISTERED_UNTIL (2999-12-31 while open).

Arguments

  • db: the database connection.

  • as_of: when a Date or DateTime, resolves DUDETAIL (latest EFFECTIVEDATE <= as_of, then highest VERSIONNO) and DUDETAILSUMMARY (the row with START_DATE <= as_of < END_DATE) as of that instant, omitting units with no such row. nothing keeps the open, latest cached version.

  • through: with as_of, the end of a window. Selects every unit registered at some instant of [as_of, through], takes its attributes from its earliest overlapping DUDETAILSUMMARY row and its DUDETAIL version in force at the later of as_of and that row's START_DATE, and spans REGISTERED_FROM and REGISTERED_UNTIL over all overlapping rows. Throws ArgumentError if a unit's REGIONID, DISPATCHTYPE or SCHEDULE_TYPE changes inside the window.

Returns

A DataFrame with one row per commissioned DUID, including CO2E_ENERGY_SOURCE.

Example

julia
db = aem_connect()
units_df = read_units(db)
source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.RegionModel.nem_network Function
julia
nem_network(db; time_series_in_memory = true, as_of = nothing, through = nothing, kwargs...) -> (sys, units)

Builds the NEM network without operation costs: buses, loads, branches, generators, batteries, scheduled loads and area interfaces. Devices are stock PowerSystems types; each dispatch device (the NEM_DISPATCH_DEVICE_TYPES components) carries a NEMUnitData with an empty NEMOfferCost. Reads no ISP cost table. units is the unit table as of as_of, or over the window [as_of, through] (see read_units).

Arguments

  • db: The database connection.

  • time_series_in_memory: Store time series in memory when true.

  • as_of: A Date or DateTime to resolve the unit and interconnector tables as of; nothing uses the latest cached version.

  • through: The end of the unit window that starts at as_of; nothing builds the units in force at as_of only.

  • kwargs...: Passed to the PowerSystems.System constructor.

Returns

A tuple (sys, units).

AustralianElectricityMarkets._add_nem_constraints! Method
julia
_add_nem_constraints!(sys, db, date_range, invoked_all, fixed; intervention = 0) -> (added, skipped)

Adds one GenericConstraint per exact (GENCONID, EFFECTIVEDATE, VERSIONNO) in invoked_all, named GENCONID@EFFECTIVEDATE#VERSIONNO and attached via add_service! to its contributing devices.

Arguments

  • sys: the System to add to.

  • db: an AEMDB connection.

  • date_range: the dispatch intervals to run.

  • invoked_all: the invoked constraint rows over date_range, as _read_constraint_inputs returns them.

  • fixed: the fixed-loading rows over date_range, as _read_constraint_inputs returns them.

  • intervention: the DISPATCHCONSTRAINT.INTERVENTION run the rows were read with (default 0).

Returns

(added, skipped): added::Vector{String} of component names, skipped::Dict{String, Symbol} mapping a skipped name to :no_definition, :no_terms, :unknown_duid, :vacuous_unknown_duid, :unknown_region, or :unknown_interconnector (the kind of the first unresolved term). Dropped unit terms are read back with get_dropped_terms.

A unit's participant fixed loading ($<DUID>) is not a generic constraint: its DISPATCHCONSTRAINT row is neither added nor reported as skipped at intervals with a fixed-loading row for an available device in sys. Devices that are unavailable or absent from sys are still reported as skipped.

Each skipped version is also recorded on sys; read it with get_skipped_constraints. The intervals of date_range with no invoked constraint (get_missing_constraint_intervals) and the constraints given the default weight 1.0 for a NULL GENERICCONSTRAINTWEIGHT (get_defaulted_constraint_weights) are recorded the same way.

A unit term whose DUID is absent from sys is dropped, as nempy does for a unit that is not in the dispatch, and recorded in the build report (get_dropped_terms) with whether DUDETAILSUMMARY registers the unit at some interval of date_range. An unresolved region or interconnector term, or a constraint with no resolvable term, skips the constraint. A constraint whose every term is a dropped unit term has a zero left-hand side; when 0 sense RHS holds at every invoked interval it cannot bind and is skipped as :vacuous_unknown_duid (its dropped terms are still recorded), otherwise it is skipped as :unknown_duid.

Throws ArgumentError when a RegionTerm resolves to a region with no Generator/Storage in sys, or when an invoked SETTLEMENTDATE falls outside date_range's grid; the throw leaves sys unmodified.

AustralianElectricityMarkets._set_band_prices! Method
julia
_set_band_prices!(sys::PSY.System) -> Nothing

Sets band_prices of each energy, FCAS and MNSP bid of sys through _day_band_prices. An energy bid takes the prices of its side's energy_offer series (loss-factor referred) over the dispatch intervals; an FCAS bid of a modelled side those of its offer_curves series, and an MNSP link bid those of its offer_curves (a static curve is its own prices), both unreferred and unrounded. Replaces each bid; repeat calls recompute the same values. Throws ArgumentError when a bid's prices vary within the dispatch range, or an FCAS bid's offer_curves is static. Requires the energy offer series.

Arguments

Returns

nothing.

AustralianElectricityMarkets._set_constraint_availability! Method
julia
_set_constraint_availability!(sys::PSY.System) -> Nothing

Sets each GenericConstraint of sys unavailable when it cannot bind over the dispatch intervals of sys: :never_invoked when its invoked series is zero at every interval (or its static invoked::Bool is false), else :no_available_device when it has contributing devices and none is available. The unavailable constraints are recorded in the build report, as get_unavailable_constraints reports them. A repeat call re-decides every constraint and replaces the recorded rows; it never makes an unavailable constraint available again. Device availability must be final before the call.

Arguments

  • sys: the system built by nem_system.

Returns

nothing.

Throws an ArgumentError if any available load or area has no demand row for an interval of date_range, or if a demand value is not finite.

Arguments

  • sys: the PowerSystems.System to add to.

  • rows: the demand rows over date_range, as read_demand returns them.

  • date_range: the dispatch intervals to run; its last timestamp ends the final interval.

  • resolution: the spacing of the intervals (default five minutes).

Returns

nothing.

julia
_set_dispatch_limits!(sys::PSY.System) -> Nothing

Adds the ramp rates and AGC ramp rates of each NEMDE unit of sys that carries telemetry: the NEM_SERIES.ramp_up_rate and NEM_SERIES.ramp_down_rate series in system-base per-unit per minute, and one fcas_series_name("fcas_agc_ramp_rate", service) series per regulation service the unit's availability supports. The ramps are the lesser of the bid and telemetered rates, a unit bid on both sides of the energy market takes its composite cross-zero rate, and a non-scheduled load is zero. A unit without telemetry gets no series.

Arguments

  • sys: the system whose telemetry set_unit_conditions! attached.

Returns

nothing.

A repeat call replaces the series.

Arguments

Returns

nothing.

_set_fcas_effective_offers!(sys)

nothing.

AustralianElectricityMarkets._set_loss_demand_coefficients! Method
julia
_set_loss_demand_coefficients!(sys::PSY.System) -> Nothing

Adds to each PowerSystems.AreaInterchange carrying exactly one InterconnectorLossModel the SingleTimeSeries NEM_SERIES.loss_demand_coefficient: at each interval, the demand term of its loss factor, loss_demand_coefficient of the region demands. A region's demand is the summed demand of the available PowerLoads in it, per unit of the system base, from each load's "loss_demand" series. The series sits on the timestamps of those series. A system whose interchanges carry no InterconnectorLossModel is left unchanged.

Arguments

  • sys: the System to add to, with its "loss_demand" load series already written.

Returns

nothing. Throws ArgumentError when the system has no available load, when an available load is on a bus with no area or has no "loss_demand" series, or when two loads' series have different timestamps.

A bid without a fixed loading writes zeros on the timestamps of its MAXAVAIL series.

Returns

nothing.

Records the unavailable devices and services of sys in its ext, as plain data, so a later change of availability can be refused by _check_nemde_availability: the NEMDE inputs (FCAS effective offers, tie-break membership, loss demand terms, constraint availability) were derived for this availability.

nothing.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets._set_nemde_forecasts! Method
julia
_set_nemde_forecasts!(sys::PSY.System) -> Nothing

Transforms the single time series of sys into five-minute forecast windows of one interval each, so the run reads one interval per step. Called last by _set_nemde_inputs!: a series added after it is not transformed, and adding one fails.

Arguments

  • sys: the system built by nem_system, whose series hold one point per stamp of its date range but the last two.

Returns

nothing.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets._set_nemde_inputs! Method
julia
_set_nemde_inputs!(sys::PSY.System) -> Nothing

Writes the NEMDE input series derived from the built inputs of sys, once and in a fixed order, after checking that its single time series are at the five-minute dispatch interval. Called by nem_system before its input checks. The writers, in order:

  • _set_referred_energy_offers!: energy offer curves, band prices referred by the side's loss factor.

  • _set_mnsp_fixed_loads!: MNSP fixed-loading value and invocation series (NEM_MNSP_FIXED_LOAD_SERIES).

  • _set_dispatch_limits!: dispatch and AGC ramp rates (NEM_SERIES).

  • _set_observed_state_inputs!: observed starting output and fixed-loading targets (NEM_STATE_INPUT_SERIES).

  • _set_fast_start_inputs!: fast-start flag, starting mode and time in mode (NEM_FAST_START_SERIES).

  • _set_fcas_effective_offers!: effective FCAS offers and regulation ramping limits.

  • _set_tie_break!: tie-break scales (tie_break_series_name) and the EnergyTieBreak service.

  • _set_loss_demand_coefficients!: loss-factor demand terms of the loss-modelled interchanges.

  • _set_constraint_availability!: marks constraints that cannot bind unavailable.

  • _set_band_prices!: band prices of each energy, FCAS and MNSP bid.

  • _set_nemde_forecasts!: transforms the single series into five-minute forecast windows; no series may be added after.

  • _set_nemde_availability!: records the unavailable devices and services the inputs were derived for.

Arguments

  • sys: the system built by nem_system.

Returns

nothing. Throws ArgumentError when a single time series of sys is not at the dispatch interval.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets._set_observed_state_inputs! Method

Adds, for each NEM dispatch device of sys whose observed starting output is a time series, the series named by NEM_STATE_INPUT_SERIES on the timestamps of that output: initial_mw in MW, zero where the build does not observe the unit. A device whose energy bid carries a fixed loading also gets fixed_load, the target in system-base per-unit, and fixed_load_invoked, 1 or 0, from _fixed_load_step_series. A device with a static starting output gets none of them.

Arguments

  • sys: the system whose observed state nem_system attached.

Returns

nothing.

AustralianElectricityMarkets._set_referred_energy_offers! Method
julia
_set_referred_energy_offers!(sys::PSY.System) -> Nothing

Adds the energy offer curves of each bidding device of sys, one series per offer side named by energy_offer_series_name. The band prices are the bid's curve prices referred to the reference node by the side's loss factor and rounded to cents. Throws ArgumentError when two FCAS bids of one service map to the same side of a unit, or when an energy bid is static rather than series-backed.

Arguments

  • sys: the system whose bids nem_system attached.

Returns

nothing.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets._set_regional_market_bids! Method
julia
_set_regional_market_bids!(sys, offers, factors, date_range; resolution = Minute(5)) -> (; added, excluded)

Gives each bidding unit of sys a MarketBidCost from the energy rows of offers (from read_offers), as set_market_bids! does on a system without NEM unit data: incremental curves from the GEN bid of a generator or storage unit, decremental curves from the LOAD bid of a scheduled load or storage unit, referred by the loss factors of factors (from read_loss_factors). A unit missing a required direction is set unavailable; a bidding unit without a loss factor throws an ArgumentError. Non-scheduled loads are left as built.

Returns

(; added, excluded), both empty: no FCAS service is added.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets._set_tie_break! Method
julia
_set_tie_break!(sys::PSY.System) -> Nothing

Adds each price-tied energy band's tie-break scale w / w_ref (its width over the widest band of its tie group at that interval, 0 when the band is untied or the group has no width) as the SingleTimeSeries tie_break_series_name of its unit, where the segment index is the band's offer segment. Adds the EnergyTieBreak named TIE_BREAK_SERVICE_NAME, with the available units that carry an energy bid as its contributing devices, once. Throws ArgumentError when a tied group is not valid. Requires the energy offer series written before it in the NEMDE input stage.

Arguments

  • sys: the System to add to.

Returns

nothing.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets._tie_break_active_bands Method
julia
_tie_break_active_bands(offers) -> Dict{Tuple{Bool, String}, Set{Int}}

The segments of each unit's offer curves that have a positive width at some timestamp, keyed (decremental, unit name). Only these can take part in a tie: a segment empty throughout, such as an unused top band priced at the Market Price Cap, would only add vacuous rows.

Returns

A Dict.

AustralianElectricityMarkets._tie_break_offers Method
julia
_tie_break_offers(sys) -> Dict

Every available component's energy offer curves, grouped by (direction, region): (decremental, region) => (stamps, resolution, offers), offers holding one (device, curves) per unit, the PiecewiseStepData curves (natural units) on stamps. Throws an ArgumentError when two curves of a group are on different timestamps.

Returns

Dict{Tuple{Bool, String}, _TieOffers}.

_to_pu(model::InterconnectorLossModel, base_power::Real) -> InterconnectorLossModel

Rescales model's MW-based fields to per-unit of base_power. breakpoints divide by base_power; loss_flow_coefficient and demand_coefficients (both 1/MW) multiply by base_power; loss_constant and from_region_loss_share are dimensionless and unchanged.

AustralianElectricityMarkets._validate_fcas_trapezium Method
julia
_validate_fcas_trapezium(t::FCASTrapezium, context::AbstractString) -> FCASTrapezium

Returns t if it is a well-formed FCAS bid trapezium (AEMO, FCAS Model in NEMDE, §2): enablement_min <= low_breakpoint <= high_breakpoint <= enablement_max and max_avail >= 0. Throws an ArgumentError naming context otherwise. A context callback is evaluated only when validation fails.

Returns invoked constraint versions that do not have a published definition in GENCONDATA. Rows with a missing GENCONID_EFFECTIVEDATE are treated as having no definition.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets._write_energy_bid! Function
julia
_write_energy_bid!(sys, device, direction, rows, grid, start_date, resolution) -> NEMEnergyBid

Writes the energy bid of device in direction from rows (its BIDPEROFFER_D and BIDDAYOFFER_D rows of that direction, from read_offers) as one series per field, named by bid_series_name, on grid, and records it in the device's NEMOfferCost. A NULL field over every row is nothing; otherwise NULL intervals and intervals without a row hold zero, except fixed_load, which holds NaN so that an unpublished loading is distinct from one of zero and is nothing where every row is NULL or zero. Throws ArgumentError for a MAXAVAIL that is missing or not finite.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets._write_fcas_bid! Method
julia
_write_fcas_bid!(sys, device, service, direction, rows, grid, start_date, resolution) -> NEMFCASBid

Writes the FCAS bid of device for service in direction from rows (its BIDPEROFFER_D and BIDDAYOFFER_D rows of that market and direction) as one series per field, named by bid_series_name, on grid, and records it in the device's NEMOfferCost. Intervals without a row hold a zero-width curve, a zero MAXAVAIL and a zero trapezium. Throws ArgumentError for a row whose trapezium is missing or out of order.

AustralianElectricityMarkets._zero_flow_constraint_definitions Method
julia
_zero_flow_constraint_definitions(gencon_versions) -> (definitions, terms)

Definition and term rows of the Interconnector Zero constraints (SVML_ZERO, VSML_ZERO, VT_ZERO, TV_ZERO) for the versions in gencon_versions, shaped like the results of read_constraint_definitions and read_constraint_terms. Each constrains one interconnector flow, factor * flow <= 0 with factor -1 or 1. Only version 2013-08-21 #1 is recognised; another version of these identifiers warns and gets no rows.

Arguments

  • gencon_versions: DataFrame with GENCONID, GENCONID_EFFECTIVEDATE, GENCONID_VERSIONNO (see read_invoked_constraints).

Returns

AustralianElectricityMarkets.add_fcas_services! Method
julia
add_fcas_services!(sys; bid_types = FCAS_BID_TYPES) -> (added, excluded)

Adds one FCASService named "<REGIONID>_<BIDTYPE>" for every region and FCAS market in bid_types with at least one available device bidding it, attached via add_service! to those devices whose bid direction the FCAS market formulation models (an incremental bid, a decremental-only bid on a Storage device or a load, or a Storage device's regulation bid on both sides). The bids are the NEMFCASBids stored by set_market_bids!. A service already in sys under that name is left as is. Devices bidding a market in a direction the formulation does not model are left out and reported.

Arguments

  • bid_types: the FCAS markets to add services for.

Returns

julia
add_nem_constraints!(sys, db, date_range; intervention::Integer = 0) -> nothing

Reads the invoked constraints and participant fixed loadings over date_range from db and attaches them to sys: one GenericConstraint per invoked version. A unit's participant fixed loading is unit offer data, excluded from the generic constraints but not attached as a series; the run formulation derives it from the bid and the unit state. Constraints skipped or dropped are recorded on sys (see get_skipped_constraints).

Arguments

  • sys: the System to add to.

  • db: an AEMDB connection.

  • date_range: the dispatch intervals to run; its last timestamp ends the final interval.

  • intervention: the DISPATCHCONSTRAINT.INTERVENTION run to read: 0 for the pricing run. 1 for the physical run where the interval has one, else the pricing run.

Returns

nothing. A second call on the same system throws an ArgumentError at the first constraint already attached.

The value of one field of bid, the NEMEnergyBid or NEMFCASBid of component, over len steps from start_time. closed_loop_input(inputs::ClosedLoopInputs, series_name, t, initial_mw) -> Union{Nothing, Any}
closed_loop_input(device, series_name, t, initial_mw, base) -> Union{Nothing, Any}

The value of the state-dependent NEMDE input series_name of the device at the interval beginning at t when the unit starts the interval at initial_mw, in the units and element type nem_system writes the series in. Returns

AustralianElectricityMarkets.closed_loop_inputs Method
julia
closed_loop_inputs(device, base) -> ClosedLoopInputs

The ClosedLoopInputs of device over the range of its observed starting output series.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.composite_ramp_rates Method
julia
composite_ramp_rates(gen_up, gen_down, load_up, load_down, period_minutes, state::NEMUnitState) -> (Float64, Float64)

The up and down ramp rates of a scheduled bidirectional unit whose output may cross zero inside the interval, MW per minute, (up, down) on the net-generation axis, where generation is positive and consumption negative. A unit that starts on the generation side raises output at its generation-side rate and one that starts on the load side lowers it at its load-side rate. A unit that would reach zero inside the interval instead ramps over the whole interval at a rate that blends the two sides, so that it finishes the interval at its own rate from zero. A NaN rate marks a side without a bid. A generation bid's ROCUP and ROCDOWN are the unit's up and down rates. A load bid's ROCUP is consumption rising, so it is the unit's down rate and its ROCDOWN is the up rate. A PowerSystems.ControllableLoad takes (ramp_up, ramp_down) = (down, up); no other device type reverses the pair. A load-only unit returns (load_down, load_up): at a non-negative start its up rate is the load ramp-down rate, and its down rate the load ramp-up rate, with no blend because it has no generation rate to compose with.

Arguments

  • gen_up, gen_down: the generation bid's ROCUP and ROCDOWN, MW/min, NaN without a generation bid.

  • load_up, load_down: the load bid's ROCUP and ROCDOWN, MW/min, NaN without a load bid.

  • period_minutes: the interval length in minutes.

  • state: the NEMUnitState at the start of the interval.

Returns

(up, down) as Float64s in MW per minute.

AustralianElectricityMarkets.fast_start_end_state Method
julia
fast_start_end_state(start_mode, time_in_mode, profile, run1_mw; interval_minutes = 5.0) -> FastStartEndState

The end state of a fast-start unit after NEMDE's commitment run. A unit starting in mode 0 is committed when its first-run energy target run1_mw is above 0 MW, entering mode 1 with 0 minutes in it. The unit then moves through modes 1, 2 and 3, once each and in that order, leaving mode k when the time left in its segment, T_k less the time in mode, is strictly less than the time left in the interval, and carrying the remainder into the next mode. The end time in mode is 0 in mode 0 and capped at T4 in mode 4; a unit never leaves mode 4.

Arguments

  • start_mode: the dispatch mode at the start of the interval, from 0 to 4.

  • time_in_mode: the minutes in start_mode at the start of the interval (fast_start_time_in_mode).

  • profile: the offer's FastStartProfile at the interval.

  • run1_mw: the unit's energy target of the first run, MW, on its offer side's axis.

  • interval_minutes: the interval length in minutes.

Returns

A FastStartEndState. Throws an ArgumentError for a start_mode outside 0 to 4.

Example

julia
profile = FastStartProfile((2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0))
fast_start_end_state(0, 0.0, profile, 10.0)  # FastStartEndState(2, 3.0, nothing)
source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.fast_start_envelope Method
julia
fast_start_envelope(end_state::FastStartEndState, profile::FastStartProfile, minimum_load) -> FastStartEnvelope

The profile bounds and ramp treatment of a fast-start unit in NEMDE's dispatch run, by its end mode, with M the minimum loading and t the end time in mode: 0 in modes 0 and 1 (the upper bound binds; the lower bound is the variable's own), M t / T2 as a fixed target in mode 2, at least M in mode 3, and at least M (1 - t / T4) in mode 4. A zero T2 gives M in mode 2 and a zero T4 gives 0 in mode 4. A unit ending in mode 0, 1 or 2 has no energy ramp rows, a unit that left mode 2 during the interval ramps up from M over the time since, and any other unit keeps its usual ramp rows.

Arguments

  • end_state: the unit's FastStartEndState.

  • profile: the offer's FastStartProfile at the interval.

  • minimum_load: the offer's MINIMUMLOAD, MW.

Returns

A FastStartEnvelope.

source

AustralianElectricityMarkets.fcas_both_sides_stranded_ok Method
julia
fcas_both_sides_stranded_ok(gen_trap, load_trap, gen_ok, load_ok, state::NEMUnitState) -> (Bool, Bool)

The stranded pre-condition of a bidirectional unit's regulation offer on both sides, as AEMO FCAS Model in NEMDE §5 states it. When both sides pass their other pre-conditions (gen_ok and load_ok), both are enabled only while the starting output lies between the load side's enablement minimum and the generation side's enablement maximum; otherwise the side that passes them is enabled only inside its own enablement span. The caller ANDs each result with that side's other §5 conditions, and a NaN starting output disables both sides.

Arguments

  • gen_trap, load_trap: the generation-side and load-side FCAS trapeziums.

  • gen_ok, load_ok: whether each side passes its other enablement pre-conditions.

  • state: the NEMUnitState at the start of the interval.

Returns

(gen_enabled, load_enabled) as Bools.

AustralianElectricityMarkets.fcas_effective_offer Method
julia
fcas_effective_offer(trap, band_widths, enabled, inactive) -> NTuple{15, Float64}

An offer that is not enabled has zero MaxAvail, slopes and widths, and enablement limits -inactive and inactive.

Arguments

  • trap: the effective FCAS trapezium of the interval, in any one unit (MW or per-unit); the slope coefficients are dimensionless.

  • band_widths: the band widths of the offer, in the unit of trap, zero-padded to FCAS_BAND_COUNT.

  • enabled: whether the offer is enabled in the interval.

  • inactive: the enablement limit of a disabled offer, in the unit of trap (FCAS_INACTIVE_LIMIT_MW converted to it).

Returns

NTuple{15, Float64}.

AustralianElectricityMarkets.fcas_preconditions_ok Method
julia
fcas_preconditions_ok(trap, total_band_width, energy_max_avail_gen, energy_max_avail_load, agc_status, is_regulation, decremental, storage) -> Bool

The computable subset of AEMO's FCAS Model in NEMDE §5 enablement pre-conditions other than the "stranded" one (fcas_state_stranded_ok or fcas_both_sides_stranded_ok, which the caller ANDs in): MaxAvail positive; at least one priced band with positive quantity; EnablementMax at or above EnablementMin; the sign pre-condition; the energy-maximum-availability pre-condition; and, for a regulation service, agc_status other than 0. The daily or profiled energy pre-condition is not checked.

The sign pre-condition requires EnablementMax >= 0 for a non-storage device, and for a storage device bidding regulation on the generation side. A storage device's load-side regulation requires EnablementMin <= 0, and its contingency FCAS carries no sign requirement.

The energy pre-condition for a non-storage device is energy_max_avail_gen >= EnablementMin. For a storage device, load-side regulation requires -energy_max_avail_load <= EnablementMax, generation-side regulation requires energy_max_avail_gen >= EnablementMin, and contingency FCAS requires both. An availability of Inf is no limit and passes, and a NaN availability is data that fails its comparison. For a storage device the caller substitutes the static output or input rating when no availability is published.

total_band_width > 0 assumes the band widths are non-negative.

Arguments

  • trap: the effective FCAS trapezium of the interval.

  • total_band_width: the sum of the offer's non-negative band widths, in the unit of trap; positive when a band carries quantity.

  • energy_max_avail_gen: the energy availability, in the unit of trap, Inf where there is no limit; for a storage device the generation-side MAXAVAIL.

  • energy_max_avail_load: the storage device's load-side MAXAVAIL, in the unit of trap, Inf where there is no limit; unused for other devices.

  • agc_status: the AGC status of the interval; -1 where unknown.

  • is_regulation: whether the service is a regulation market.

  • decremental: whether the offer is the load side of the device.

  • storage: whether the device is a PowerSystems.Storage.

Returns

Bool.

julia

The joint energy and FCAS limit of one direction: state.initial_mw plus the AGC ramping capability on the upper form (energy is dispatched and the regulation side delivered) and minus it on the lower form. A PowerSystems.ControllableLoad's LOWERREG row takes the upper form (fcas_upper_regulation_service). capability and the result are in the same unit as state.initial_mw.

Arguments

  • capability: the AGC ramping capability over the interval.

  • upper: whether the limit is the upper form.

  • state: the NEMUnitState at the start of the interval.

Returns

A Float64.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.fcas_ramping_limits Method
julia
fcas_ramping_limits(capability, bdu_capability, enabled, upper, fast_start, inactive, state::NEMUnitState) -> NTuple{2, Float64}

One interval of a regulation market's ramping limits, in the unit of inactive: (joint, bdu). joint is the AEMO FCAS Model in NEMDE §6.1 right-hand side, fcas_ramping_limit of the AGC ramping capability on the upper or lower form, and ±inactive where the row is inactive: the capability is zero or absent, the unit is not enabled for the market, or the unit is exempt on a fast-start interval (fast_start_ramp_exempt). bdu is the §6.4 right-hand side of a PSY.Storage device bidding both sides, its AGC ramping capability on the market, and inactive where that is zero. A caller with an unknown starting output writes ±inactive itself.

Arguments

  • capability: the AGC ramping capability over the interval, in the unit of inactive; 0.0 where the ramp rate is absent.

  • bdu_capability: the AGC ramping capability of a device bidding both sides, in the unit of inactive; 0.0 otherwise. Must not be NaN: callers clean a NaN capability to 0.0.

  • enabled: whether the unit is enabled for the market in the interval.

  • upper: whether the joint limit is the upper form.

  • fast_start: whether the unit carries a fast-start inflexibility profile in the interval.

  • inactive: the inactive limit (FCAS_INACTIVE_LIMIT_MW converted to the unit of the capabilities and of state).

  • state: the NEMUnitState at the start of the interval, its initial_mw in the unit of the capabilities.

Returns

NTuple{2, Float64}.

AustralianElectricityMarkets.interconnector_losses Method
julia
interconnector_losses(model, flow, demand) -> Float64

MW lost on model at flow, the integral of loss_factor(model, f, demand) - 1 over [0, flow]:

julia
(loss_constant - 1 + Σ_r demand_coefficients[r] * demand[r]) * flow
    + 0.5 * loss_flow_coefficient * flow^2

LOSSCONSTANT is a loss factor quoted relative to unity, hence the - 1.

julia
observed_unit_states(device, stamps::AbstractVector{DateTime}) -> Vector{NEMUnitState}

The state of device at the start of the interval beginning at each stamp of stamps, read from its NEMObservedState. A stamp with a finite dispatch mode gives its observed output and mode, and the time in mode of fast_start_time_in_mode from the observed mode time and the fast-start profile of the device's energy offer at the stamp. A stamp with a non-finite mode gives zero output in mode 0 when the build does not observe the unit there (outside the device's registration, or a pinned non-scheduled load), and the observed output in mode 0 when the previous interval is unobserved, which is the device's first registered interval. The time in mode is zero in mode 0.

Arguments

  • device: the NEM device.

  • stamps: the first timestamps of the intervals, consecutive at the series' resolution.

Returns

A Vector{NEMUnitState} the length of stamps. Throws an ArgumentError naming device and the stamp when device has no NEM observed state, when the dispatch mode is not finite at a stamp whose previous interval is observed, or when the mode time of a fast-start unit in modes 1 to 4 is not finite.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.scale_fcas_trapezium Method
julia
scale_fcas_trapezium(trapezium; agc_enablement_min = nothing, agc_enablement_max = nothing,
    agc_max_avail = nothing, uigf = nothing, is_regulation) -> FCASTrapezium

Applies AEMO FCAS Model in NEMDE §4's trapezium scaling to the offered trapezium: the AGC enablement limits (§4.1) and AGC ramping capability (§4.2) for a regulation trapezium (is_regulation), and the UIGF ceiling (§4.3) for a semi-scheduled unit. Each bound is replaced only when the corresponding input is more restrictive than the bid's own value, and the paired breakpoint slides to keep that side's slope angle (low_breakpoint with enablement_min, high_breakpoint with enablement_max) equal to the bid's. The breakpoints are never clamped, so a squeezed result can have high_breakpoint < low_breakpoint (a trapezium whose peak lies below max_avail) or enablement_max < enablement_min (no feasible FCAS).

A nothing or 0.0 agc_enablement_min, agc_enablement_max or agc_max_avail is treated as absent: no scaling on that leg. uigf has no such exemption: 0.0 clamps enablement_max to zero, matching a semi-scheduled unit's weather forecast of no output.

Arguments

  • trapezium: the offered FCASTrapezium.

  • agc_enablement_min, agc_enablement_max: telemetered AGC enablement limits, in trapezium's units. Regulation only.

  • agc_max_avail: telemetered AGC ramping capability (ramp rate × dispatch interval), in trapezium's units. Regulation only.

  • uigf: the semi-scheduled unit's weather ceiling, in trapezium's units, or nothing for a scheduled unit.

  • is_regulation: whether trapezium is a RAISEREG/LOWERREG trapezium.

Returns

An FCASTrapezium.

TOTALDEMAND becomes the "max_active_power" series and LOSSDEMAND (see read_demand) a second "loss_demand" series. Throws an ArgumentError if any available load or area has no demand row for an interval of date_range, or if a demand value is not finite. A second call on the same system throws an ArgumentError for the series already attached.

Arguments

  • kwargs: Additional keyword arguments passed to read_demand.

Returns

AustralianElectricityMarkets.set_interconnector_flow_limits! Method
julia
set_interconnector_flow_limits!(sys, db, date_range; kwargs...)

Attaches the per-interval flow limits of read_interconnector_limits to every PSY.AreaInterchange in sys as a NEMInterconnectorLimits whose keys are the SingleTimeSeries named by NEM_INTERCONNECTOR_SERIES, in MW: the flow is bounded below by IMPORTLIMIT and above by EXPORTLIMIT. The lower bound is the smaller of the two limits and the upper bound the larger, each clamped into the static envelope [-MAXMWIN, MAXMWOUT]. An interval with no published row or a missing limit keeps the static limit, and one @warn counts them.

The published limits are computed after NEMDE's solve (each binding constraint's right-hand side projected with the other terms held at the solved values), so bounding flow by them pins it to NEMDE's answer. Use them as a diagnostic, not when validating flows.

A repeat call replaces the earlier limits.

Arguments

  • sys: the System to add to.

  • db: an AEMDB connection.

  • date_range: the dispatch intervals to run.

  • kwargs: passed to read_interconnector_limits (e.g. intervention).

Returns

nothing.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.set_market_bids! Method
julia
set_market_bids!(sys, db, date_range; markets = NEM_MARKETS, resolution = Minute(5)) -> (; added, excluded)

Stores the bids of each unit of sys for date_range. On a NEMDE system (units carrying NEM unit data, built by nem_network or nem_system(db, NEMDEConfiguration(); date_range)) it is one read_offers read of the markets, written as one series per bid field (bid_series_name) and recorded on the unit's NEMOfferCost as NEMEnergyBids and NEMFCASBids. The values are as offered: MW, $/MWh at the connection point and MW/min. A unit's loss factors, from which AEMSim refers its energy prices, are on its NEMRegistration recorded by nem_network.

On a system without NEM unit data, such as one built with RegionalNetworkConfiguration, only the energy bids are read and each bidding unit gets a MarketBidCost for PowerSimulations' own formulations: the incremental offer curves of its GEN bid and the decremental curves of its LOAD bid, as SingleTimeSeries in natural units. Each curve's prices are divided by the unit's loss factor from read_loss_factors, so they are referred to the regional reference node, and its quantity is capped at the interval's MAXAVAIL. FCAS bids are not read and no service is added.

Generators bid GEN. Scheduled loads bid LOAD, and a non-scheduled load bids no energy; an available one gets a zero MAXAVAIL series of the LOAD energy bid name instead. Storage devices bid both directions. A unit missing a required energy direction is set unavailable. A device bidding a required direction at a stamp of its registration without a row throws. FCAS bids are recorded for every unit, and the FCAS services of markets are added by add_fcas_services!. A non-scheduled load with an FCAS bid is made available when it is commissioned. Repeat calls replace the series and the bids of the same direction and service.

Arguments

  • sys: The PowerSystems.System object, with NEM unit data attached to the bidding units.

  • db: The database connection.

  • date_range: The intervals to read (half-open, the last stamp exclusive).

  • markets: The BidTypes to read; defaults to NEM_MARKETS.

  • resolution: The spacing of the series, which must match the intervals of date_range.

Returns

(; added, excluded) as add_fcas_services! returns them.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.set_mnsp_offers! Method
julia
set_mnsp_offers!(sys, db, date_range; intervention = 0) -> Vector{String}

Attaches the offers and link data of each available MNSP interconnector. Standing INTERCONNECTORCONSTRAINT.ICTYPE data determines which interconnectors require offers.

Each PSY.AreaInterchange of an MNSP receives, per direction, a NEMMNSPLink (the link's registration) and a NEMMNSPBid whose keys hold the cumulative price bands and their MAXAVAIL in MW, the RAMPUPRATE in MW/min as published, and the FIXEDLOAD in MW, NaN where it is NULL (a numeric zero is an active fixed loading of zero). The forward link's METEREDMWFLOW in MW, selected by intervention, is held by a NEMMNSPObservedState. The forward link's direction is the interchange's from_area to its to_area.

Every link must have complete, valid inputs on the five-minute interval grid; missing or invalid inputs, or an ICTYPE that differs between the first and last interval, throw ArgumentError before any offers in sys are changed. Calling it again replaces earlier data, which requires transform_single_time_series! not to have run yet.

Arguments

  • sys: the PSY.System to add to.

  • db: an AEMDB connection holding MNSP registration, offers and dispatch bid tracking.

  • date_range: five-minute interval-ending timestamps, with an exclusive final timestamp.

  • intervention: the run of the metered flow: 0 for the pricing run. 1 for the physical run where the interval has one, else the pricing run.

Returns

The names of the interconnectors that received offers. Regulated interconnectors require none.

AustralianElectricityMarkets.set_regional_availability! Method
julia
set_regional_availability!(sys, db, date_range; resolution::Dates.Period = Minute(30), intervention::Integer = 0)

Attaches a "max_active_power" series to every available RenewableGen and HydroGen in sys, for the economic studies of a RegionalNetworkConfiguration. Unlike set_unit_conditions!, a unit with no DISPATCHLOAD rows is not an error: each stamp takes the first of these values that exists:

  1. a RenewableGen with a read_uigf row: UIGF / capacity;

  2. a read_dispatch_limits AVAILABILITY row: AVAILABILITY / capacity;

  3. a solar (PVe) or wind (WT or WS) RenewableGen: the regional semi-scheduled UIGF of its area, the DISPATCHREGIONSUM SS_SOLAR_UIGF or SS_WIND_UIGF, over the summed NATURAL capacity of the region's semi-scheduled units of that fuel, clamped to [0, 1]. The denominator counts every such unit in sys that has UIGF rows, available or not;

  4. otherwise 1.0, the registered capacity.

Every value is clamped to [0, 1]. A device with a capacity of zero or less is 0.0 at every stamp. The series is per-unit of each device's own max_active_power. A repeat call replaces the series. Thermal, storage and load devices are not touched.

Arguments

  • sys: the System to add to.

  • db: an AEMDB connection.

  • date_range: the intervals to build. Only its first and last values are used, as the half-open first(date_range) <= t < last(date_range). The first value must be a multiple of resolution on the epoch grid, or an ArgumentError is thrown.

  • resolution: the spacing of the stamps. Defaults to 30 minutes.

  • intervention: 0 for the pricing run. 1 for the physical run where the interval has one, else the pricing run.

Returns

nothing.

Example

julia
db = aem_connect()
sys = nem_system(db, RegionalNetworkConfiguration())
set_regional_availability!(sys, db, Date(2025, 1, 2):Date(2025, 1, 3))

AustralianElectricityMarkets.set_unit_conditions! Method
julia
set_unit_conditions!(sys, db, date_range; intervention = 0)

Attaches each available NEM dispatch device's operating condition from one read_unit_conditions read. The values are SingleTimeSeries in AEMO's natural units, and their keys are held in the device's NEMTelemetry and NEMObservedState:

  • "telemetry_agc_status": AGCSTATUS, 0 or 1.

  • "telemetry_uigf": UIGF, MW, for a semi-scheduled unit only.

  • "telemetry_ramp_up_limit", "telemetry_ramp_down_limit": RAMPUPRATE, RAMPDOWNRATE, MW/h.

  • "telemetry_raise_reg_enablement", "telemetry_lower_reg_enablement": the (min, max) MW enablement of each regulation service.

  • "telemetry_raise_reg_max_avail", "telemetry_lower_reg_max_avail": RAISEREGAVAILABILITY, LOWERREGAVAILABILITY, MW.

  • "observed_initial_mw": INITIALMW, MW, zero where no row is published.

  • "observed_dispatch_mode": DISPATCHMODE of the previous interval, the fast-start mode at the start of each interval.

  • "observed_dispatch_mode_time": DISPATCHMODETIME of the previous interval, the minutes in that mode at the start of each interval.

A non-scheduled load is pinned to zero initial output, but keeps its metered ramp rates for AGC ramping. The read also covers the interval before the first, which supplies the first dispatch mode. A ramp, regulation or AGC status value with no row at an interval is NaN, and so is a dispatch mode or mode time whose previous interval has no row; the telemetry uigf is zero there. A registered unit with a NaN mode is refused by the NEMDE state. Every problem across every device is raised as one ArgumentError, and sys is left unmodified. A repeat call replaces each series it writes, and replaces the structs on the devices.

The series are read through the keys, and AEMSim derives the dispatch inputs from them. The schedule type and registration span of a device come from its NEMRegistration.

Arguments

  • sys: the System to add to, after set_market_bids! has made the non-scheduled loads with FCAS bids available.

  • db: an AEMDB connection.

  • date_range: the five-minute dispatch intervals to run, including the exclusive stop timestamp.

  • intervention: the DISPATCHLOAD run: 0 for the pricing run. 1 for the physical run where the interval has one, else the pricing run.

Returns

nothing.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.side_suffix Method
julia

AustralianElectricityMarkets.tie_groups Method
julia
tie_groups(bands) -> Vector{Vector{Int}}

Price-tied groups of bands (each with price, name and band): runs of the bands sorted by price whose consecutive prices differ by at most TIE_BREAK_CVP_FACTOR, kept when they hold bands of two or more units. Each group lists indices into bands in sorted order. Throws an ArgumentError for a run spanning more than TIE_BREAK_CVP_FACTOR, which only transitive ties produce.

Returns

Vector{Vector{Int}}.
