AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations ​

NEMDE run in PowerSimulations.jl: dispatch problems, device, FCAS, constraint and loss formulations, the problem template and sequence, and the readers of solved results.

AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FAST_START_COMMITMENT_NAME Constant
julia
FAST_START_COMMITMENT_NAME

The name of the commitment run's decision model in nem_dispatch_sequence: "fast_start_commitment".

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMDE_HIGHS_OPTIONS Constant
julia
NEMDE_HIGHS_OPTIONS

The HiGHS options of the NEMDE problem: relative MIP gap 1e-8, absolute MIP gap 1e-10, and the root sub-MIP heuristics (RINS, RENS, root reduced cost and feasibility jump) turned off.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._VIOLATION_TOLERANCE_MW Constant

MW of slack below which a constraint row counts as satisfied.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.AbstractNEMDispatch Type
julia
AbstractNEMDispatch

Supertype for the NEM dispatch device formulations: a per-band bid stack, a per-interval ramp limit, and separately priced energy availability limits, applied to one active power variable per device. A scheduled load (PowerSystems.ControllableLoad) uses the same variable as consumed MW, priced on its decremental offer and withdrawn from the area balance.

Methods are defined over PowerSystems.StaticInjection; a PowerSimulations.ProblemTemplate selects the component types they apply to. Subtypes differ only in what the ramp constraint measures against; NEMDispatch is the one subtype. Ramp, availability, offer-total and fixed-loading rows always carry priced slacks; the device model's use_slacks does not apply to them. The energy offer cost and the slack penalties are objective terms only; no PowerSimulations cost expression is built, and slack penalties are reported as violation rows of a run's results rather than as device cost.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.AbstractNEMDispatchProblem Type
julia
AbstractNEMDispatchProblem <: PSI.DefaultDecisionProblem

The PSI decision problems of a NEM dispatch dispatch interval. The concrete problem type selects the run mode: NEMDispatchProblem runs each interval from AEMO's observed state, and NEMClosedLoopDispatchProblem from the previous solved interval.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.AreaBalanceSlack Type
julia
AreaBalanceSlack

Variable type of the regional demand-supply balance slacks, keyed by PSY.Area with meta "deficit" (demand left unserved, added to the balance as supply) or "surplus" (excess generation, removed from it). System-base per-unit.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.EnergyBandWidthParameter Type
julia
EnergyBandWidthParameter

Time-series parameter of an energy offer's band widths in MW, read from the device's energy_offer series (energy_offer_decremental for meta "load"), with bands beyond an interval's offer at width 0.0. Meta "gen" or "load".

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.EnergyLimitTimeSeriesParameter Type
julia
EnergyLimitTimeSeriesParameter

Time-series parameter of an energy limit in system-base per-unit: the raw bid MAXAVAIL, with key meta "max_avail", or a semi-scheduled unit's UIGF, with key meta "uigf".

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.EnergyOfferBandVariable Type
julia
EnergyOfferBandVariable

Variable type of a device's cleared MW in each band of its energy offer, in system-base per-unit, keyed (name, label, t) with band labels "1" to "n". Meta "gen" for a generation-side offer and "load" for a consumption-side offer; a band beyond an interval's offer has zero width.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASBandWidthParameter Type
julia
FCASBandWidthParameter

Time-series parameter of a device's effective FCAS offer band widths for one market and side, read from its "fcas_effective_<BIDTYPE>[_decremental]" series, per-unit of the system base, with a band axis "1" to "10" (FCAS_BAND_COUNT). Keyed by device type with meta "<BIDTYPE>[_decremental]".

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASCapacityVariable Type
julia
FCASCapacityVariable

Variable type for a contributing device's enabled FCAS capacity in one FCASService, bounded above by the device's MAXAVAIL for that market and interval. For a PSY.Storage device bidding a regulation market on both sides, this is not used; see FCASSideCapacityVariable/FCASUnitRegulationTarget.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASJointCapacityConstraint Type
julia
FCASJointCapacityConstraint

Constraint type for one side (named "<service>_upper"/"<service>_lower" in its container key, or "<service>_gen_upper"/"<service>_gen_lower"/"<service>_load_upper"/ "<service>_load_lower" for a PSY.Storage device bidding a regulation market on both sides) of the AEMO FCAS Model in NEMDE §6.2/§6.3 joint capacity constraint, bounding a device's FCASJointCapacityLHS against its FCAS trapezium's enablement window.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASJointCapacityLHS Type
julia
FCASJointCapacityLHS

Expression type for one side (named "<service>_upper"/"<service>_lower" in its container key, or "<service>_gen_upper"/"<service>_gen_lower"/"<service>_load_upper"/ "<service>_load_lower" for a PSY.Storage device bidding a regulation market on both sides) of the AEMO FCAS Model in NEMDE §6.2/§6.3 joint capacity constraint's left-hand side, per (device, t): energy dispatch and any matching regulation term. The service's own trapezium slope term is added in the FCASJointCapacityConstraint row, with its coefficient driven by FCASUpperSlopeParameter or FCASLowerSlopeParameter.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASLowerSlopeParameter Type
julia
FCASLowerSlopeParameter

Constraint-coefficient parameter of a device's effective FCAS LowerSlopeCoeff for one market and side, the negated coefficient of its FCAS capacity in the lower FCASJointCapacityConstraint row, read from its "fcas_effective_<BIDTYPE>[_decremental]" series. Keyed by device type with meta "<BIDTYPE>[_decremental]".

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASMarket Type
julia
FCASMarket

Formulation for an FCASService, co-optimising FCAS capacity alongside energy. Band costs and slack penalties are objective terms only, not part of any PowerSimulations cost expression.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASOfferBandVariable Type
julia
FCASOfferBandVariable

One band of a contributing device's FCAS offer at one timestep, non-negative and per-unit of the system base. Indexed (device name, band label, t) with the meta of the capacity variable it sums to: the service name, or "<service>_gen"/"<service>_load" for a PSY.Storage device's two regulation sides. The band axis is sized to the most bands any of those offers has over the system's series; a band an offer does not have at an interval has zero width.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASOfferLimitParameter Type
julia
FCASOfferLimitParameter

Time-series parameter of a device's effective FCAS offer limits for one market and side, read from its "fcas_effective_<BIDTYPE>[_decremental]" series (fcas_effective_series_name), per-unit of the system base, with a field axis "max_avail", "enablement_min", "enablement_max". Keyed by device type with meta "<BIDTYPE>[_decremental]".

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASRampingLimitParameter Type
julia
FCASRampingLimitParameter

Time-series parameter of a device's regulation ramping limits for one regulation market, read from its "fcas_ramping_limits_<BIDTYPE>" series (fcas_ramping_series_name), per-unit of the system base, with a field axis "joint_ramping" (FCASUnitConstraint right-hand side) and "bdu_ramping" (FCASUnitConstraint right-hand side). Keyed by device type with meta "<BIDTYPE>".

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASSideCapacityVariable Type
julia
FCASSideCapacityVariable

Variable type for one side (named "<service>_gen"/"<service>_load" in its container key) of a PSY.Storage device's regulation capacity, when it bids that market on both the generation and load sides, bounded above by that side's own scaled MAXAVAIL.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASSlack Type
julia
FCASSlack

Variable type for the elastic slacks of the FCASMarket rows, built when the owning PSI.ServiceModel has use_slacks = true. The key meta is "<variant>|<meta>": the variant first, then the row's own container meta.

  • "joint_capacity|<meta>": a FCASJointCapacityConstraint row (AEMO xxUpperDeficit/xxLowerSurplus), priced at FCAS_CAPACITY_CVP_FACTOR times the Market Price Cap.

  • "joint_ramping|<service>": a joint ramping row of FCASUnitConstraint (AEMO R5REJointRampDeficit/L5REJointRampDeficit), priced at FCAS_RAMPING_CVP_FACTOR.

  • "max_avail|<meta>": a MaxAvail row of FCASUnitConstraint, priced at FCAS_MAXAVAIL_CVP_FACTOR.

  • "bdu_ramping|<service>": a BDU ramping row of FCASUnitConstraint, priced at FCAS_BDU_RAMPING_CVP_FACTOR.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASUnitConstraint Type
julia
FCASUnitConstraint

Constraint type for the per-unit FCAS rows of FCASMarket, indexed (device name, t). The key meta is "<row>|<meta>": the row first, then the row's own container meta.

  • "max_avail|<service>_maxavail" (or "_gen_maxavail"/"_load_maxavail"): the MaxAvail limit on a FCASCapacityVariable or FCASSideCapacityVariable. The row is elastic when the owning PSI.ServiceModel has use_slacks = true.

  • "offer_band|<group meta>": Σ bands == capacity for one contributing device's FCAS offer, its FCASOfferBandVariables summing to its capacity variable.

  • "joint_ramping|<service>": AEMO FCAS Model in NEMDE §6.1's joint ramping constraint, bounding a contributing device's net energy dispatch combined with its FCASUnitRegulationTarget against its telemetered AGC ramp from InitialMW.

  • "bdu_ramping|<service>": AEMO FCAS Model in NEMDE §6.4's BDU regulating FCAS SCADA ramping constraint, bounding a PSY.Storage device's FCASUnitRegulationTarget against the device's SCADA ramping capability.

Its dual, when requested, is recorded for the "joint_ramping" rows only.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASUnitRegulationTarget Type
julia
FCASUnitRegulationTarget

Expression type for a device's total regulation FCAS target in one FCASService, per (device, t): FCASCapacityVariable for a device bidding one side, or the sum of both FCASSideCapacityVariables for a PSY.Storage device bidding both sides. This is what AEMO FCAS Model in NEMDE §6.2's joint capacity constraint, the BDU and joint ramping rows of FCASUnitConstraint read as "Raise Regulation FCAS Target"/"Lower Regulation FCAS Target".

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FCASUpperSlopeParameter Type
julia
FCASUpperSlopeParameter

Constraint-coefficient parameter of a device's effective FCAS UpperSlopeCoeff for one market and side, the coefficient of its FCAS capacity in the upper FCASJointCapacityConstraint row, read from its "fcas_effective_<BIDTYPE>[_decremental]" series. Keyed by device type with meta "<BIDTYPE>[_decremental]".

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FastStartCommitmentTargetParameter Type
julia
FastStartCommitmentTargetParameter

The affected value of the dispatch run's PSI.FixValueFeedforward in nem_dispatch_sequence: the FixValueParameter the feedforward adds carries the commitment run's energy targets, which set the fast-start rows, and fixes no variable.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FastStartModeTimeSeriesParameter Type
julia
FastStartModeTimeSeriesParameter

Time-series parameter of the starting fast-start dispatch mode of each unit with a fast-start profile (has_fast_start_profile), read from the "fast_start_start_mode" series of NEM_FAST_START_SERIES. A model of a fast-start run (nem_dispatch_sequence) adds it, and its per-step update sets the unit's fast-start rows for the interval.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FixedLoadInvokedTimeSeriesParameter Type

Time-series parameter that is 1 at the intervals a unit's fixed loading applies and 0 elsewhere.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.FixedLoadTimeSeriesParameter Type

Time-series parameter of a unit's participant fixed loading, net injection in system-base per-unit.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.GenericConstraintInvocationParameter Type
julia
GenericConstraintInvocationParameter

Constraint-bound parameter holding the invocation (1.0/0.0) of a GenericConstraint per interval, read at each simulation step from the constraint's invoked series. The row of an invoked interval has its bounds and the row of a non-invoked interval is free (-Inf, Inf).

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.GenericConstraintSlackDown Type
julia
GenericConstraintSlackDown

Variable type for the elastic slack absorbing a GenericConstraint's left-hand side below its right-hand side limit, built only when LinearFactorLimit's sense is GE or EQ and the owning PSI.ServiceModel has use_slacks = true. Merged into NEMConstraintLHS with multiplier +1.0.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.GenericConstraintSlackUp Type
julia
GenericConstraintSlackUp

Variable type for the elastic slack absorbing a GenericConstraint's left-hand side above its right-hand side limit, built only when LinearFactorLimit's sense is LE or EQ and the owning PSI.ServiceModel has use_slacks = true. Merged into NEMConstraintLHS with multiplier -1.0.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.InitialPowerTimeSeriesParameter Type
julia
InitialPowerTimeSeriesParameter

Time-series parameter for a device's "initial_mw_seed" series, in MW; the parameter's multiplier converts it to system-base per unit.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.InterconnectorFlowSlack Type
julia
InterconnectorFlowSlack

Variable type for the elastic slack on an interconnector's flow limits, per (interconnector, t) in MW per-unit of the system base. The key meta names the variant: "surplus" relaxes the upper limit (AEMO's FlowSurplus) and "deficit" the lower limit (AEMO's FlowDeficit). Both are priced at INTERCONNECTOR_FLOW_CVP_FACTOR times the Market Price Cap.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.InterconnectorLossConstraint Type
julia
InterconnectorLossConstraint

Row over one interconnector, per-unit. The key meta names the row, and a composite meta continues after its first |:

  • "flow_segment": flow[ic,t] == first_breakpoint + sum(segment flows), indexed (interconnector name, t).

  • "loss_definition": loss[ic,t] == losses at the first breakpoint + sum(segment slope * segment flow) + k[t] * flow[ic,t], with segment slopes and first-breakpoint losses at zero demand and k[t] the LossDemandCoefficientParameter. Indexed (interconnector name, t).

  • "segment_order|ub" and "segment_order|lb": contiguous segment fill. Segment s + 1 may carry flow only when segment s is full (ub), and segment s is full when its fill indicator is on (lb). Indexed (interconnector name, segment label, t).

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.InterconnectorLossSegmentFullVariable Type

Binary: segment s of an interconnector's loss curve is completely filled at one timestep. Indexed (interconnector name, segment label, t), with labels 1:(max segments - 1); cells beyond an interconnector's own segments - 1 appear in no constraint.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.InterconnectorLossSegmentVariable Type

One loss-curve segment's flow allocation for one interconnector at one timestep, in MW per-unit. Indexed (interconnector name, segment label, t); the segment axis is sized to the largest interconnector's segment count, and a smaller interconnector's unused cells are fixed to 0.0.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.InterconnectorLossVariable Type

An interconnector's total loss at one timestep, in MW per-unit of base power.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.LinearFactorLimit Type
julia
LinearFactorLimit

Formulation for a GenericConstraint: assembles NEMConstraintLHS from the constraint's own stored terms and bounds it against NEMConstraintRHSParameter with a NEMConstraintLimit. Slack penalties are objective terms only, not part of any PowerSimulations cost expression. Every constraint of a model shares one container per role (expression, limit, dual, parameters and each slack direction), with the constraint name as the first axis and an empty key meta.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.LossDemandCoefficientParameter Type
julia
LossDemandCoefficientParameter

Coefficient of an interconnector's flow in its "loss_definition" InterconnectorLossConstraint at each interval: the demand term Σ_r demand_coefficients[r] × demand[r] of its loss factor, read from the "loss_demand_coefficient" series that nem_system writes.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.MNSPBandWidthParameter Type
julia
MNSPBandWidthParameter

Time-series parameter of an MNSP link's offered band widths, in MW, read from its "link_<direction>_offer" series with a band axis; bands beyond an interval's offer have width 0.0. Meta "forward" or "reverse" names the link.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.MNSPLinkBandVariable Type
julia
MNSPLinkBandVariable

One MNSP link's flow in one offer band at one timestep, non-negative and per-unit of the system base. Indexed (interconnector name, band label, t) with meta "forward" or "reverse"; the band axis is sized to the most bands any link offers over the system's series, and a band a link does not offer at an interval has zero width.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.MNSPLinkConstraint Type
julia
MNSPLinkConstraint

Row over one MNSP link or interconnector, per-unit. The key meta names the row, and a composite meta continues after its first |:

  • "flow": flow[ic,t] == forward link flow - reverse link flow, indexed (interconnector name, t).

  • "band": Σ bands + offer surplus == link flow, indexed (interconnector name, "forward" | "reverse", t).

  • "max_avail": link flow - availability surplus <= MAXAVAIL, indexed as "band".

  • "direction": link flow <= bound * on, where on is MNSPLinkDirectionVariable for the forward link and its complement for the reverse link, indexed as "band".

  • "loss|lb" and "loss|ub": bound one link's MNSPLinkLossVariable to zero when the link is inactive, loss >= lower * on and loss <= upper * on, indexed as "band".

  • "loss_split": forward loss + reverse loss == interconnector loss, indexed (interconnector name, t).

  • "ramp|up" and "ramp|down": the signed net-flow ramp limit about metered starting flow, indexed (interconnector name, t).

  • "fixed_load|<link>_upper" and "fixed_load|<link>_lower": the link's fixed-loading limit, with the MNSPSlack surplus or deficit it relaxes, indexed (interconnector name, t).

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.MNSPLinkDirectionVariable Type
julia
MNSPLinkDirectionVariable

Binary per interconnector and timestep, 1 when only the forward link may flow and 0 when only the reverse link may, so the two links never flow at once.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.MNSPLinkFlowVariable Type
julia
MNSPLinkFlowVariable

One MNSP link's flow at one timestep, non-negative and per-unit of the system base. Indexed (interconnector name, "forward" | "reverse", t); the forward link carries flow from the interconnector's from area to its to area.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.MNSPLinkLossVariable Type
julia
MNSPLinkLossVariable

DC losses supplied by one directional MNSP link's sending area, per-unit of the system base. Indexed (interconnector name, "forward" | "reverse", t); the two directions sum to the interconnector's total loss, and only the active direction is nonzero.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.MNSPMaxAvailParameter Type
julia
MNSPMaxAvailParameter

Time-series parameter of an MNSP link's MAXAVAIL, in MW, read from its "link_<direction>_max_avail" series. Meta "forward" or "reverse" names the link.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.MNSPOperatingParameter Type
julia
MNSPOperatingParameter

Time-series parameter of an MNSP operating input in natural units. The key meta names the input:

  • "initial_flow": the signed metered starting flow, in MW, from the NEMMNSPObservedState key NEM_MNSP_SERIES.initial_flow.

  • "forward_ramp_rate": the forward link ramp rate, in MW/min, from the forward bid's ramp_up key.

  • "reverse_ramp_rate": the reverse link ramp rate, in MW/min, from the reverse bid's ramp_up key, which limits the net flow's decrease.

  • "forward_fixed_load" and "reverse_fixed_load": the link's fixed loading, in MW, read from the NEM_MNSP_FIXED_LOAD_SERIES value series that nem_system writes from the bid's fixed_load; the bid's raw series holds NaN where AEMO publishes NULL, and the written series holds 0 there.

  • "forward_fixed_load_invoked" and "reverse_fixed_load_invoked": the fixed-loading invocation flag, 1 where the bid publishes a loading and 0 where it is NULL, read from the invoked series that nem_system writes.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.MNSPSlack Type
julia
MNSPSlack

Non-negative violation of an MNSP operating constraint, in system-base per-unit MW. The key meta names the variant, followed by its link direction for the commercial limits and fixed loading:

  • "max_avail|<link>": excess over the link's availability.

  • "offer|<link>": flow above the cleared offered bands.

  • "ramp|up" or "ramp|down": excess over, or shortfall below, the net-flow ramp limit.

  • "fixed_load|surplus|<link>" or "fixed_load|deficit|<link>": excess over, or shortfall below, the link's fixed-loading target.

The link is "forward" or "reverse".

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMClosedLoopDispatchProblem Type
julia
NEMClosedLoopDispatchProblem <: AbstractNEMDispatchProblem

The closed-loop NEM dispatch problem: the first interval starts from AEMO's observed state, and each later interval of a Simulation from the previous interval's solved output. The starting output of each unit and the starting flow of each MNSP are NEMInitialPower and NEMInitialFlow initial conditions, and the inputs derived from that state (battery ramp rates, fixed loadings, effective FCAS offers and regulation ramping limits) are recomputed each step. Fast-start dispatch modes keep their observed values.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMConstraintBoundParameter Type

Time-series parameter that frees (value 0) or bounds (nonzero) a constraint row; see _add_bound_target!.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMConstraintCoefficientParameter Type

Time-series parameter whose value is the coefficient of a variable in a constraint row; see _add_coefficient_target!.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMConstraintLHS Type
julia
NEMConstraintLHS

Expression type for a GenericConstraint's accumulated affine left-hand side, Σ FACTOR·variable.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMConstraintLimit Type
julia
NEMConstraintLimit

Constraint type bounding a GenericConstraint's NEMConstraintLHS expression against its run right-hand side.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMConstraintRHSParameter Type
julia
NEMConstraintRHSParameter

Time-series parameter type for a GenericConstraint's right-hand side, fed from its right-hand side time series, in MW.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMDispatch Type
julia
NEMDispatch

AbstractNEMDispatch whose ramp constraint measures against the device's initial MW at every interval, read from the observed state series NEM_STATE_INPUT_SERIES. Intervals are decoupled.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMDispatchProblem Type
julia
NEMDispatchProblem <: AbstractNEMDispatchProblem

The open-loop NEM dispatch problem: every interval starts from AEMO's observed initial MW and MNSP flows. Building it checks the template against the system and prices the area-balance slacks and every penalty at the Market Price Cap, resolved from the model's initial time unless the model sets one.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMFloatTimeSeriesParameter Type
julia
NEMFloatTimeSeriesParameter

Abstract supertype of the time-series parameters whose values are stored as Float64 in every build mode, because they are written into constraint coefficients and row bounds rather than used as JuMP parameters.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMInitialFlow Type
julia
NEMInitialFlow <: PSI.InitialConditionType

The starting flow of an MNSP in a closed-loop run, in MW: the metered flow at the first interval, then the previous interval's solved flow.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMInitialPower Type
julia
NEMInitialPower <: PSI.InitialConditionType

The starting output of a NEMDE unit in a closed-loop run, in system-base per-unit (net of charging for a battery): AEMO's observed output at the first interval, then the previous interval's solved output.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMInterconnectorLoss Type
julia
NEMInterconnectorLoss

Device formulation for PSY.AreaInterchange that apportions the attached InterconnectorLossModel's segment losses between its two areas. Supports PSI.AreaBalancePowerModel only, matching NEMDE's regional balance; other network models, missing or ambiguous loss models and concave curves throw ArgumentError. The demand term of each interval's loss factor is read from the interchange's "loss_demand_coefficient" series (written by nem_system) as a LossDemandCoefficientParameter, so the formulation also runs in recurrent simulations.

Notes

Loss follows the breakpoint interpolation at every price sign: segments fill contiguously from the first breakpoint, enforced by binary fill indicators when an interconnector has more than one segment. The breakpoint range also bounds flow, with a warning when it is narrower than the device's static flow limits. Flow-limit rows always carry priced slacks; the device model's use_slacks does not apply to them. Slack penalties and MNSP band costs are objective terms only, not part of any PowerSimulations cost expression.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMInterconnectorLossless Type
julia
NEMInterconnectorLossless

Device formulation for PSY.AreaInterchange with the same flow variable, flow limits and priced flow slacks as NEMInterconnectorLoss, and the balance terms only: -flow at the from area and +flow at the to area. It has no loss variables, loss curve or MNSP link offers, so an MNSP is a regulated flow within its limits. Supports PSI.AreaBalancePowerModel only; other network models throw ArgumentError.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMUnitConstraint Type
julia
NEMUnitConstraint

Constraint type of the unit rows of an AbstractNEMDispatch formulation, one container per device type and row. The key meta names the row, composed with the row's own container meta after a |:

  • "offer_band|gen" and "offer_band|load": dispatch == Σ bands + surplus - deficit for one device and interval, over its EnergyOfferBandVariables. The part after | is the offer's side, "gen" or "load".

  • "max_avail", "uigf", "max_avail_out" and "max_avail_in": the energy availability rows, the dispatch less its surplus at most the live limit. "max_avail_in" is the charging side of a battery.

  • "fixed_load|upper" and "fixed_load|lower": AEMO's Energy Inflexible Offer rows (Schedule of Constraint Violation Penalty Factors v8.0, item 13, "Unit = X MW") holding a unit's net energy at its fixed loading.

  • "fast_start|lower", "fast_start|upper" and "fast_start|ramp_up": a fast-start unit's rows in the dispatch run of nem_dispatch_sequence, the energy target at least the profile's lower bound, at most its upper bound, and at most the minimum loading plus the ramp-up since the unit left mode 2.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.NEMUnitSlack Type
julia
NEMUnitSlack

Non-negative elastic slack of a unit row under an AbstractNEMDispatch formulation, one container per device type and variant. The key meta is "<family>|<variant>":

  • energy offer ("energy_offer|..."): surplus, deficit, decremental_surplus and decremental_deficit, the dispatch above or below the cleared incremental or decremental energy bands.

  • energy limit ("energy_limit|..."): max_avail, uigf, max_avail_out and max_avail_in, the dispatch above a raw or forecast availability limit.

  • fixed load ("fixed_load|..."): surplus and deficit, the net energy above or below a fixed loading.

  • unit ramp ("unit_ramp|..."): up and down, the excess over a ramp rate's base.

  • fast-start profile ("fast_start|..."): lower and upper, the energy target below or above a fast-start unit's inflexibility profile in the dispatch run of nem_dispatch_sequence.

Slacks are in system-base per-unit; results read in MW.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.RampDown Type

Direction tag of the "down" RampRateTimeSeriesParameter.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.RampRateTimeSeriesParameter Type
julia
RampRateTimeSeriesParameter

Time-series parameter for a device's ramp-rate series, in system-base per-unit per minute. The key meta names the direction: "up" reads the "ramp_up_rate" series, "down" the "ramp_down_rate" series.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.RampUp Type

Direction tag of the "up" RampRateTimeSeriesParameter.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.TieBreakConstraint Type
julia
TieBreakConstraint

Constraint type of the tie-break rows s_b x_a - s_a x_b + up - down = 0, in a sparse container keyed like TieBreakSlackUp.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.TieBreakMarket Type
julia
TieBreakMarket

Formulation for an EnergyTieBreak: one elastic row per pair of price-tied energy bands of different contributing units, dispatching the bands of a tie group in proportion to their size.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.TieBreakScaleParameter Type
julia
TieBreakScaleParameter

Constraint-coefficient parameter of one energy offer band's tie-break scale w / w_ref, the band's width over the widest band of its price-tied group, read from the device's "tie_break_scale_<k>[_decremental]" series (written by nem_system). In the tie-break row of bands a and b, band b's scale is the coefficient of a's cleared MW and minus band a's scale that of b's. Keyed by device type with meta "<k>[_decremental]", k being the segment index on the offer curve.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.TieBreakSlackDown Type
julia
TieBreakSlackDown

Variable type for the downward slack of a tie-break row, keyed like TieBreakSlackUp.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.TieBreakSlackUp Type

TieBreakSlackUp

Variable type for the upward slack of a tie-break row, in system-base per-unit MW, keyed (label, pair, t) with label the region and direction ("<region>_offer" or "<region>_bid") and pair the row's index among that label's rows at time step t.

_FCASOfferGroup

One capacity variable container of an FCASService and the offers summing to it: the container's meta, its capacity variable type and offers, a vector of (device, decremental).

source
PowerSimulations.DecisionModel Method
julia
PSI.DecisionModel{M}(template, sys, jump_model = nothing; name = "dispatch", market_price_cap = nothing, fast_start_run = nothing, kwargs...) where {M <: AbstractNEMDispatchProblem} -> PSI.DecisionModel{M}

Constructs the one-interval NEM dispatch model of template on sys. The horizon, resolution and interval are one dispatch interval, and the "closed_loop" setting records whether M is NEMClosedLoopDispatchProblem. Extra keyword arguments are passed to PSI.Settings, e.g. optimizer and initial_time.

Arguments

  • template: a PSI.ProblemTemplate, e.g. template_nemde().

  • sys: the system the template is checked against when the model is built.

  • jump_model: the JuMP.Model to build into, or nothing.

  • name: the name of the decision problem, used to retrieve its results.

  • market_price_cap: a Market Price Cap in $/MWh that replaces the one dated by the initial time, or nothing.

  • fast_start_run: :commitment or :dispatch for a run of NEMDE's two-run fast-start dispatch (see nem_dispatch_sequence), or nothing for a single run without fast-start rows.

  • area_balance_slacks: true replaces the network model's own balance slacks of an AreaBalancePowerModel by AreaBalanceSlack at the Market Price Cap. With false, or with a network model other than AreaBalancePowerModel, PowerSimulations' own balance slacks are kept at PowerSimulations' default cost.

  • kwargs...: keyword arguments of PSI.Settings. Passing ext, horizon, interval or resolution throws ArgumentError; use market_price_cap for the cap.

Returns

A PSI.DecisionModel{M}. An invalid market_price_cap or fast_start_run throws ArgumentError.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_fcas_prices Method
julia
read_fcas_prices(results, sys::PSY.System; resolution = nothing) -> DataFrame

Maps solved NEMConstraintLimit duals onto regional FCAS prices: each (region, service) ROP is the sum of the duals of every built GenericConstraint whose get_fcas_requirements names that pair, in $/MWh. This mirrors the sum of DISPATCH_FCAS_REQ's MARGINALVALUE in the published FCAS prices. Duals keep the solver's sign (change in cost per unit increase of the right-hand side): non-negative for a binding >= constraint, non-positive for <=. Warns when a constraint with requirements has no recorded dual.

Arguments

  • results: PSI.OptimizationProblemResults of a model, or PSI.SimulationProblemResults of a simulation (its realized duals), that recorded NEMConstraintLimit duals.

  • sys: the System the model was built from.

  • resolution: interval length converting per-interval duals to $/MWh. Defaults to the resolution the results record, which a single-interval solve does not; required then.

Returns

A DataFrame with SETTLEMENTDATE, REGIONID, BIDTYPE and ROP, the same columns as read_published_interval reports for FCAS prices.

source
AustralianElectricityMarkets.Readers.read_prices Method
julia
read_prices(results, sys::PSY.System) -> DataFrame

Reads the solved regional prices of a PSI model from the duals of its CopperPlateBalanceConstraint rows, one row per region and interval. The dual is per unit of interval energy, so it is divided by the base power and the interval length to give $/MWh. Throws when a price is not finite.

Arguments

  • results: PSI.OptimizationProblemResults of a model, or PSI.SimulationProblemResults of a simulation (its realized duals).

  • sys: the System the model was built from.

Returns

A DataFrame with SETTLEMENTDATE, REGIONID and ROP, the same columns as the prices of read_published_interval.

AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._add_area_balance_slacks! Method
julia
_add_area_balance_slacks!(container, sys, network_model)

Adds the AreaBalanceSlack deficit and surplus to each area's ActivePowerBalance, priced at AREA_BALANCE_CVP_FACTOR times the Market Price Cap. Called from the argument stage of every AEMSim formulation that writes to the area balance, so it runs before the balance row is built. For an AreaBalancePowerModel and unless the "area_balance_slacks" setting is false, it turns PSI's own balance slacks off on the build's network model and adds the slacks once per container. A template with no such formulation never calls it and keeps the caller's use_slacks.

Arguments

  • container: the PSI.OptimizationContainer being built.

  • sys: the system the build runs on.

  • network_model: the network model of the build; mutated to turn off its own balance slacks.

Returns

nothing.

julia
_add_bound_target!(container, key, name, t, constraint, active)

Register the interval bounds active of constraint as driven by cell (name, t) of the constraint-bound parameter under key: the row is free where the parameter value times its multiplier is zero and has bounds active elsewhere. Each call adds a target, so repeated calls for one cell duplicate it.

Arguments

  • key::PSI.ParameterKey: key of a parameter with T <: NEMConstraintBoundParameter.

  • name::String: component name on the parameter's first axis.

  • t::Int: time step.

  • constraint::JuMP.ConstraintRef: constraint built as a MOI.Interval row.

  • active::NTuple{2, Float64}: lower and upper bound of the row when it is active.

Returns

nothing.

Register the coefficient of variable in constraint as driven by cell (name, t) of the constraint-coefficient parameter under key, and set it to scale * value * multiplier from the current parameter values. Each call adds a target, so repeated calls for one cell duplicate it.

julia
_add_energy_offer_bands!(container, devices, model, side)

Prices the energy offer of the devices of model that carry the energy_offer series of side: one EnergyOfferBandVariable per band (labelled "1" to "n"), bounded by its EnergyBandWidthParameter width, summing with the offer's surplus and deficit slacks to the dispatch variable the side prices (NEMUnitConstraint rows under meta "offer_band|<side>"), and costed in the invariant objective at the band price times the system base power and the interval hours, negative on the LOAD side. Band prices are the band_prices of each device's energy bid, the loss-factor referred day prices. Devices without the series add nothing.

Arguments

AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._add_fast_start_rows! Method
julia
_add_fast_start_rows!(container, devices, model::PSI.DeviceModel{T})

Adds the fast-start rows of the units of devices with a fast-start profile (has_fast_start_profile) in a fast-start run, and nothing in a single run or for a battery. Both runs add a FastStartModeTimeSeriesParameter, whose per-step update resets the rows. The dispatch run also adds the "fast_start|lower", "fast_start|upper" and "fast_start|ramp_up" rows of NEMUnitConstraint, the first two with NEMUnitSlack slacks priced at FAST_START_CVP_FACTOR times the Market Price Cap and the third sharing the unit's "unit_ramp|up" slack. The rows are then set for the build's initial time (_set_fast_start_rows!).

Returns

nothing.

AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._add_fcas_capacity_constraints! Method
julia
_add_fcas_capacity_constraints!(container, model, devices, label, capacity, metas)

Builds the MaxAvail and joint capacity rows (_add_fcas_capacity_rows!) of each of devices at every time step, on its capacity variable and the FCASJointCapacityLHS expressions of meta "<label>_upper" and "<label>_lower". The FCASUnitConstraint MaxAvail rows take the meta "max_avail|<label>_maxavail", and the FCASJointCapacityConstraint containers the metas "<label>_upper" and "<label>_lower". Their FCASSlacks take the same metas after the variant prefix.

Arguments

  • devices: the devices sharing the capacity variable container capacity.

  • label: the service name, suffixed with the side for a PSY.Storage device bidding both sides.

  • metas: each device's offer meta (_fcas_offer_meta), in the order of devices.

Returns

nothing.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._add_fcas_capacity_rows! Method
julia
_add_fcas_capacity_rows!(container, device, meta, capacity, upper_lhs, lower_lhs, slacks, cons, dname, t)

Builds device's MaxAvail row and its two AEMO FCAS Model in NEMDE §6.2/§6.3 joint capacity rows at t for the offer meta (_fcas_offer_meta) with capacity variable capacity: capacity - slack <= MaxAvail, upper_lhs + UpperSlopeCoeff × capacity - slack <= EnablementMax and lower_lhs - LowerSlopeCoeff × capacity + slack >= EnablementMin. The limits come from FCASOfferLimitParameter and the slope coefficients from FCASUpperSlopeParameter and FCASLowerSlopeParameter.

Arguments

  • slacks: (max, upper, lower) slack containers, each nothing without slacks.

  • cons: (max, upper, lower) constraint containers.

Returns

nothing.

_add_fcas_energy_terms!(container, expr, device, is_regulation, decremental, dname, t)

Builds AEMO FCAS Model in NEMDE §6.1's joint ramping rows of FCASUnitConstraint for every contributing device of a regulation FCASService named name: the unit's net energy (_energy_variables) combined with its FCASUnitRegulationTarget against the "joint_ramping" field of its FCASRampingLimitParameter, in the upper or lower form depending on bid_type (fcas_upper_regulation_service). Where §6.1 does not apply, the parameter holds FCAS_INACTIVE_LIMIT_MW and the row never binds.

nothing.

AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._add_fixed_load_costs! Method

Prices the fixed-loading slacks of devices at FIXED_LOADING_CVP_FACTOR times the Market Price Cap of the build's initial interval.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._add_flow_limit_constraint! Method
julia
_add_flow_limit_constraint!(container, devices, device_model, network_model)

Bounds PSI.FlowActivePowerVariable by the static flow_limits, or by the from-to and to-from flow-limit parameters when every device carries those time series. Each row carries an InterconnectorFlowSlack with meta "surplus" (upper) or "deficit" (lower) priced at INTERCONNECTOR_FLOW_CVP_FACTOR times the Market Price Cap, always, whatever the device model's use_slacks, as NEMDE's limit is always soft, so limits that conflict with each other, or with the loss breakpoint range under NEMInterconnectorLoss, are violated at that price instead of making the model infeasible. Under NEMInterconnectorLoss the breakpoint range itself stays a hard bound. Because the slacks are priced from the Market Price Cap of the build's initial interval, building requires a cap for that interval, whether the cap comes from MARKET_PRICE_CAP_BY_FINANCIAL_YEAR (from FY2021-22) or from the "market_price_cap" entry of the model's settings, even when use_slacks is false.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._add_gc_slack_variables! Method

_add_gc_slack_variables!(container, gc, model)

Fills GenericConstraintSlackUp/GenericConstraintSlackDown for gc in the shared slack containers when PSI.get_use_slacks(model), one side per get_sense(gc) (LE → up only, GE → down only, EQ → both), and merges each into NEMConstraintLHS: -slack_up on the LE side, +slack_down on the GE side, so add_constraints!'s stored bound becomes satisfiable by relaxing it rather than infeasible. A no-op when use_slacks is false.

_add_loss_variables!(container, devices, loss_models)

Devices carrying directional MNSP offers omit the balance terms: their losses are supplied at the sending area. The segment axis is sized to the largest interconnector; unused cells are fixed to zero. All quantities are per-unit of the system base.

AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._add_mnsp_link_constraints! Method
julia
_add_mnsp_link_constraints!(container, devices, device_model)

Adds, for each device in devices carrying MNSP offers, the rows over the variables of _add_mnsp_link_variables!: each band within its offered width, the bands plus an offer surplus summing to the link flow (meta "band"), an elastic MAXAVAIL limit ("max_avail"), flow = forward - reverse ("flow"), one direction at a time ("direction"), each directional loss zero on the inactive link ("loss|lb" and "loss|ub"), and the two losses summing to the interconnector loss ("loss_split"), all rows of MNSPLinkConstraint.

Adds, for each device in devices carrying MNSP offers, the MNSP parameters, a link flow, band and loss variable per direction and timestep, and a direction binary per timestep. Link flows enter the regional balances at the link's ends, and each directional loss at its sending area, bounded by _loss_range. Devices without offers keep their free-flow model.

Arguments

  • container: the optimization container of the model being built.

  • devices: the PSY.AreaInterchange devices of the formulation.

Returns

nothing.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._add_mpc_penalty! Method
julia
_add_mpc_penalty!(container, V, T, names, cvp_factor; meta, rate = nothing)

Prices the slack variables of the container keyed (V, T, meta) for names at cvp_factor times the Market Price Cap per MW of one dispatch interval, as a constant of the invariant objective. The cap is rate when given, else _container_market_price_cap at the container's initial time: a simulation keeps the cap of its first interval, since its range lies within one financial year.

Arguments

  • container: the PSI.OptimizationContainer being built.

  • V, T, meta: the key of the slack variable container, indexed [name, t], in system-base per-unit.

  • names: the names of the slack container to price.

  • cvp_factor: the AEMO CVP factor of the constraint the slack relaxes.

  • rate: a Market Price Cap that replaces the dated one, or nothing.

Returns

nothing.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._add_nem_ramp_constraints! Method
julia
_add_nem_ramp_constraints!(container, T, devices, net_at, base_accessor)

Holds each device's dispatch net_at(name, t) within its per-interval ramp rates of its base. Rates are read from the "ramp_up_rate" and "ramp_down_rate" parameters in system-base per-unit per minute and multiplied by the interval length in minutes. Each PSI.RampConstraint row carries a NEMUnitSlack of the unit_ramp|up or unit_ramp|down variant, priced at UNIT_RAMP_CVP_FACTOR times the Market Price Cap, so conflicts with the availability limits are resolved through the competing violation costs.

Arguments

  • container: the PSI.OptimizationContainer being built.

  • T: the component type of devices.

  • devices: the devices whose rows are added.

  • net_at: (name, t) -> the device's dispatch expression at interval t.

  • base_accessor: names -> a (name, t) -> accessor of the base each row measures against.

Returns

nothing.

AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._check_nemde_constraint_inputs Method
julia
_check_nemde_constraint_inputs(sys; scope = :all)

Verifies that the constraint-build records of sys are complete: no missing dispatch constraint interval, no defaulted weight, no skipped constraint, and no dropped unit term of a registered unit. A vacuous constraint is skipped, but its dropped terms fail when the unit is registered over the range. Defaulted weights and dropped terms are judged only for the constraints of scope; a record naming no GenericConstraint of sys is always judged. Skipped constraints and missing intervals are always judged.

Arguments

  • sys: the PSY.System to check.

  • scope: the constraint scope of the template, :all or :fcas_requirements, as _in_constraint_scope reads it.

Returns

nothing. Throws an ArgumentError naming the first incomplete input.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._check_nemde_system_inputs Method
julia
_check_nemde_system_inputs(sys, template)

Verifies that sys carries every input the run of template depends on, from the records of the setters that built it: with a GenericConstraint service model, get_missing_constraint_intervals, get_defaulted_constraint_weights, get_skipped_constraints and get_dropped_terms of the constraint build (DISPATCHCONSTRAINT, GENCONDATA, SPDCONNECTIONPOINTCONSTRAINT, SPDREGIONCONSTRAINT, SPDINTERCONNECTORCONSTRAINT); the dispatch-limit series of the dispatch-limits build (DISPATCHLOAD) on every dispatch device, the resolution and five-minute alignment of the series keyed by each device's NEMObservedState; and, with an NEMInterconnectorLoss interchange model, the offers of set_mnsp_offers! (INTERCONNECTORCONSTRAINT, MNSP_INTERCONNECTOR, MNSP_DAYOFFER, MNSP_BIDOFFERPERIOD, DISPATCH_MNSPBIDTRK) on every available MNSP.

Arguments

  • sys: the PSY.System to check.

  • template: the PSI.ProblemTemplate the run builds.

  • has_limits: the predicate for a device's dispatch-limit series, _has_nem_dispatch_limits by default.

Returns

nothing. Throws an ArgumentError naming the first incomplete input and how to supply it.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations._set_fast_start_rows! Method
julia
_set_fast_start_rows!(container, T, start_time::DateTime)

Sets the fast-start rows of the units of type T for the window from start_time, from AEM's fast_start_unit_inputs. In the commitment run, a unit exempt by fast_start_ramp_exempt (fast-start and starting in mode 0, 1 or 2) has its energy ramp rows relaxed. In the dispatch run, the unit's end state (fast_start_end_state) of the commitment run's target gives its fast_start_envelope: the profile rows take the envelope's bounds, both ramp rows are relaxed for :none, the ramp-up row is replaced by the "fast_start|ramp_up" row at fast_start_ramp_up_limit for :from_minimum_load, and both keep their built bounds for :standard. A unit that is not fast-start at an interval keeps its ramp rows and has its profile rows relaxed.

Returns

nothing.

model with its breakpoints reduced to at most loss_breakpoints: the first and last are kept and the interior is taken evenly by index. Returns model itself when loss_breakpoints is nothing or not below its breakpoint count, and throws ArgumentError when loss_breakpoints is below 2.

Arguments

  • model: the InterconnectorLossModel of an interchange.

  • loss_breakpoints: nothing or the largest number of breakpoints to keep.

Returns

An InterconnectorLossModel.

AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.check_fcas_services Method
julia
check_fcas_services(template, sys)

Verifies every available FCASService that template models under FCASMarket is buildable: each available contributing device's type is modeled by a PSI.DeviceModel whose formulation dispatches energy (not PSI.FixedOutput), the device's FCAS bid direction is one FCASMarket models (incremental on any device but a load, decremental on a PSY.Storage device or a load, both only on a PSY.Storage device's regulation market), no device contributes to more than one such FCASService of the same market, and a regulation contributor with a positive AGC ramp rate also keys an observed initial MW series, which AEMO FCAS Model in NEMDE §6.1's joint ramping constraint needs. A per-interval gap in the observed initial MW is not checked.

Arguments

  • template: PSI.ProblemTemplate to check device coverage against.

  • sys: system to read services and components from.

Returns

nothing. Throws ArgumentError naming every problem device otherwise.

julia
compare_intervals(published::NamedTuple, solved::NamedTuple) -> NamedTuple

Joins the published outcome of a set of intervals onto its solved outcome, one row per published key. Solved values a model does not produce are missing.

Arguments

  • published: the outcome from read_published_interval over the intervals.

  • solved: the outcome from read_solved_interval over the same intervals.

Returns

A named tuple of DataFrames keyed as solved: prices (by REGIONID), dispatch (by DUID), interconnectors (by INTERCONNECTORID) and fcas_prices (by REGIONID and BIDTYPE). Each has the published and solved values in <column>_published and <column>_solved, sorted by SETTLEMENTDATE and its key.

AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.comparison_summary Method

comparison_summary(comparison::NamedTuple) -> DataFrame

Summarises the paired solved and published values of each table of a compare_intervals result, one row per metric: energy_price, dispatch_mw, interconnector_flow_mw, interconnector_losses_mw and fcas_price.

A DataFrame with columns metric, n_rows, n_paired, n_missing, n_nonfinite, mae, rmse, max_abs_gap and bias. Rows with a missing or non-finite side are counted and left out of the error statistics, which are missing when no row pairs. bias is the mean solved minus published.

AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.nem_dispatch_sequence Method
julia
nem_dispatch_sequence(::Type{M}, template, sys; name = "dispatch", commitment_name = FAST_START_COMMITMENT_NAME, fast_start = true, ini_cond_chronology = PSI.InterProblemChronology(), kwargs...) where {M <: AbstractNEMDispatchProblem} -> NamedTuple

The decision models of a NEM dispatch run of template on sys and the PSI.SimulationSequence that runs them. When an available unit of a non-battery device type that template models under an AbstractNEMDispatch formulation has a fast-start profile (has_fast_start_profile), every interval runs NEMDE's two dispatch runs at the same timestamp. The commitment run, named commitment_name, leaves out the energy ramp rows of the fast-start units starting in mode 0, 1 or 2. The dispatch run, named name, reads the commitment run's energy targets through a PSI.FixValueFeedforward and holds each fast-start unit to the inflexibility profile of its end mode, elastic at FAST_START_CVP_FACTOR times the Market Price Cap, with the ramp rows of that end mode. Prices and results are the dispatch run's. Without a fast-start unit, or with fast_start = false, the sequence holds one model, named name, built as PSI.DecisionModel{M} builds it, with no inflexibility profile.

Arguments

  • M: NEMDispatchProblem or NEMClosedLoopDispatchProblem.

  • template: a PSI.ProblemTemplate, e.g. template_nemde(); each model builds from its own copy.

  • sys: the NEMDE system, built by nem_system(db, NEMDEConfiguration(); date_range).

  • name: the name of the dispatch run, whose results a run reads.

  • commitment_name: the name of the commitment run.

  • fast_start: run NEMDE's two fast-start runs when sys has a fast-start unit; false builds the single model.

  • ini_cond_chronology: the initial-condition chronology of the sequence.

  • kwargs...: keyword arguments of PSI.DecisionModel{M}, e.g. optimizer, initial_time and market_price_cap, given to both models.

Returns

A NamedTuple of models (the PSI.SimulationModels), sequence (the PSI.SimulationSequence), dispatch (the dispatch run's PSI.DecisionModel{M}) and commitment (the commitment run's model, or nothing for a single model).

Example

julia
(; models, sequence, dispatch) = nem_dispatch_sequence(NEMDispatchProblem, template_nemde(), sys;
    optimizer = nemde_optimizer(), initial_time = first(steps))
simulation = PSI.Simulation(; name = "run", steps = length(steps), models, sequence,
    simulation_folder = mktempdir(), initial_time = first(steps))

Returns

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.read_constraint_violations Method
julia
read_constraint_violations(results, sys::PSY.System) -> DataFrame

Reads every elastic slack above tolerance of a PSI model, in every interval and every family of the slack table. A generic constraint's slack counts only at the intervals where it is invoked. Rows are sorted by DateTime, family, name, variable and direction.

The families are "energy_offer", "energy_max_avail", "energy_uigf", "fixed_load", "mnsp_max_avail", "mnsp_offer", "mnsp_ramp", "mnsp_fixed_load", "unit_ramp", "fast_start_profile", "interconnector_flow", "fcas_max_avail", "fcas_bdu_ramping", "fcas_joint_ramping", "fcas_enablement", "generic_constraint" and "area_balance". direction is "up" for a slack relaxing a <= row and "down" for one relaxing a >= row; for "area_balance", an equality, "up" is a deficit (demand left unserved) and "down" a surplus. The tie-break slacks are not listed.

Arguments

  • results: PSI.OptimizationProblemResults of a model, or PSI.SimulationProblemResults of a simulation, whose realized values are read.

  • sys: the System the model was built from.

Returns

A DataFrame with family, name, DateTime, MW, direction and variable (the slack variable's key as PSI encodes it in result files, e.g. "NEMUnitSlack__HydroDispatch__unit_ramp|up"; a generic constraint's slack key is followed by "__" and the constraint name). The unit ramp rows are those with family == "unit_ramp".

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.read_interconnector_loss_gaps Method
julia
read_interconnector_loss_gaps(results, sys::PSY.System) -> DataFrame

Reads each interconnector's solved loss against the loss curve at its solved flow, for every interval with a solved flow. The reference is the full curve stored on the System, so under loss_breakpoints gap_mw also includes the thinning error (the solver used the thinned curve), and it can be negative. gap_mw is zero where the solved loss equals the full curve.

Arguments

  • results: PSI.OptimizationProblemResults of a model using NEMInterconnectorLoss, or PSI.SimulationProblemResults of a simulation (its realized values).

  • sys: the System the model was built from.

Returns

A DataFrame with columns interconnector, DateTime, flow_mw, solved_loss_mw, curve_loss_mw, gap_mw (MW) and weighted_loss_price ($/MWh), where weighted_loss_price is share * ROP_from + (1 - share) * ROP_to from read_prices. The table is empty when the results hold no interchange flow or no InterconnectorLossVariable, as in a lossless run.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.read_solved_interval Method
julia
read_solved_interval(results, sys::PSY.System) -> NamedTuple

Reads the solved outcome of a PSI model over every interval of results, in the keys and columns of read_published_interval so that solved and published outcomes compare by a join. Solved prices carry ROP only, with no RRP.

Arguments

  • results: PSI.OptimizationProblemResults of a model, or PSI.SimulationProblemResults of a simulation, whose realized values are read.

  • sys: the System the model was built from.

Returns

A named tuple of DataFrames:

  • prices: SETTLEMENTDATE, REGIONID, ROP, from read_prices.

  • dispatch: SETTLEMENTDATE, DUID, TOTALCLEARED, the net MW of each unit.

  • interconnectors: SETTLEMENTDATE, INTERCONNECTORID, MWFLOW, MWLOSSES; empty when the results hold no FlowActivePowerVariable for PSY.AreaInterchange. MWLOSSES is missing when the results hold no InterconnectorLossVariable.

  • fcas_prices: SETTLEMENTDATE, REGIONID, BIDTYPE, ROP, from read_fcas_prices.

Throws when a regional price is not finite.

template_energy_only() -> PSI.ProblemTemplate

It leaves out the other generic constraints and tie-break. It corresponds to nempy example 5. Run it with fast_start = false, as in nem_dispatch_sequence(NEMDispatchProblem, template_fcas(), sys; fast_start = false).

AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.template_interconnected Method
julia
template_interconnected() -> PSI.ProblemTemplate

The energy run with the interchanges lossless: template_energy_only plus each PSY.AreaInterchange under NEMInterconnectorLossless, so its flow limits apply and no loss is taken. It leaves out losses, FCAS, generic constraints and tie-break, and an MNSP is a regulated flow within its limits. It is the lossless counterpart of nempy example 3, whose constant percentage loss is not modelled here. Run it with fast_start = false, as in nem_dispatch_sequence(NEMDispatchProblem, template_interconnected(), sys; fast_start = false).

Returns

A PSI.ProblemTemplate.

AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.template_losses Method
julia
template_losses(; loss_breakpoints = nothing) -> PSI.ProblemTemplate

The energy run with the interchanges under NEMInterconnectorLoss: template_energy_only plus the dynamic loss model of each interchange. It leaves out FCAS, generic constraints and tie-break. It corresponds to nempy example 4. Run it with fast_start = false, as in nem_dispatch_sequence(NEMDispatchProblem, template_losses(), sys; fast_start = false).

Arguments

  • loss_breakpoints: nothing, or an integer N >= 2 keeping at most N breakpoints of each loss model, as in template_nemde.

Returns

A PSI.ProblemTemplate.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.template_nemde Method
julia
template_nemde(;
    interconnectors = :losses, fcas = true, constraints = true, tie_break = true,
    exclude_constraints = Dict{String, Symbol}(), loss_breakpoints = nothing,
) -> PSI.ProblemTemplate

The keyword builder of the dispatch templates. The default builds the PSI.ProblemTemplate that models NEMDE dispatch: NEMDispatch for each type of NEM_DISPATCH_DEVICE_TYPES, including the batteries, PSI.StaticPowerLoad demand, NEMInterconnectorLoss on each PSY.AreaInterchange, an FCASMarket per FCASService, a LinearFactorLimit per GenericConstraint and the TieBreakMarket service model, over PSI.AreaBalancePowerModel regions. The balance slacks are PSI's own here; the build replaces them by AreaBalanceSlack, priced at the Market Price Cap, because this template holds AEMSim formulations.

Each keyword removes or swaps one part. The presets template_energy_only, template_interconnected, template_losses, template_fcas and template_constraints are calls to this builder with fixed keywords. check_template_against_sys, check_fcas_services and template_skipped_constraints read what is modeled from the template they are given.

Arguments

  • interconnectors: :losses models each PSY.AreaInterchange under NEMInterconnectorLoss, :lossless under NEMInterconnectorLossless and :none leaves the interchanges out.

  • fcas: whether the FCASMarket service model of each FCASService is included.

  • constraints: true models every GenericConstraint, :fcas_requirements only those carrying FCAS requirements (it needs fcas = true, since FCAS requirements are constraints that clear nothing without the FCAS market), and false none.

  • tie_break: whether the TieBreakMarket service model is included.

  • exclude_constraints: a Dict from the names of GenericConstraints to the reason each is recorded with. The run leaves these constraints out without changing the system; an unknown name fails the model's template validation. Needs constraints other than false. Default empty.

  • loss_breakpoints: nothing reads every breakpoint of each interchange's loss model. An integer N >= 2 keeps at most N of them, always the first and last and the interior thinned evenly by index, and applies to the interchange model at build without changing the system. Needs interconnectors = :losses.

Returns

A PSI.ProblemTemplate.

source
AustralianElectricityMarketsSimulations.template_skipped_constraints Method
julia
template_skipped_constraints(sys, template) -> DataFrame

The GenericConstraints of sys that a run of template leaves out, without changing sys or template. The rows are the constraints unavailable from the build (get_unavailable_constraints, with n_missing = 0), the available constraints the template excludes by name, with n_missing = 0, and every other available constraint the template cannot build, with the number of failing terms. A template with no GenericConstraint service model reports the unavailable constraints only. Available constraints outside the template's constraint scope (with constraints = :fcas_requirements, those without FCAS requirements) are left out of the run by design, so they are neither reported nor diagnosed. Out-of-scope constraints that are unavailable still appear among the unavailable rows. It reads the caller's template or the expanded template of a built model alike.

Arguments

  • sys: the NEMDE system built by nem_system.

  • template: the PSI.ProblemTemplate the run builds, e.g. template_nemde().

Returns

A DataFrame with columns constraint, reason and n_missing, sorted by constraint name.

PowerSimulations.add_constraints! Method
julia
PSI.add_constraints!(container, ::Type{NEMUnitConstraint}, devices, model::PSI.DeviceModel{T, <:AbstractNEMDispatch}, network_model)

Adds AEMO's Energy Inflexible Offer rows (Schedule of Constraint Violation Penalty Factors v8.0, item 13, "Unit = X MW") for the devices carrying a fixed loading: the device's net energy (_energy_variables) minus its surplus slack at most, and plus its deficit slack at least, its fixed loading. At an interval with no fixed loading both rows are relaxed by _FIXED_LOAD_INACTIVE_MW, so they never bind.

PowerSimulations.construct_service! Method
julia
PSI.construct_service!(container, sys, ::PSI.ModelConstructStage, model::PSI.ServiceModel{EnergyTieBreak, TieBreakMarket}, devices_template, incompatible_device_types, network_model)

Model stage for TieBreakMarket: adds one TieBreakConstraint row s_b x_a - s_a x_b + up - down = 0 per pair of bands of different units in a price-tied group, the energy offer bands of one region, direction and time step whose prices at the reference node are within TIE_BREAK_CVP_FACTOR of one another. x is a band's cleared MW and s its TieBreakScaleParameter; the TieBreakSlackUp and TieBreakSlackDown slacks, in system-base per-unit MW, are priced at TIE_BREAK_CVP_FACTOR $/MWh. FCAS bands are not tied. Groups are read once at build and held for every step. Containers are keyed by EnergyTieBreak with the service name as meta and are not added when no band is tied. Throws an ArgumentError unless the nem_system NEMDE inputs covered every tied band and every contributor carrying a scale is modelled or excluded by its device model's "filter_function".

Returns

nothing.

PowerSimulations.get_default_time_series_names Method
julia
PSI.get_default_time_series_names(::Type{<:PSY.StaticInjection}, ::Type{<:AbstractNEMDispatch})

Registers the time series AbstractNEMDispatch reads as parameters, each under its fixed series name. RampRateTimeSeriesParameter is registered once: its two directions are added with their own series names. EnergyLimitTimeSeriesParameter is added once per meta, each with its own series name, so its entry names the MAXAVAIL series only as a default. The initial-power and fixed-loading parameters are added explicitly from the build's first-solve seed series, so they take no entry here.

Returns

A Dict mapping each PowerSimulations.TimeSeriesParameter type to its series name.

Registers the time series AbstractNEMDispatch reads as parameters for a battery: the ramp parameters and the generation and consumption energy bid MAXAVAIL series. The initial-power parameter is added explicitly from the build's first-solve seed series. Both availability limits carry priced violations on the generation and consumption axes. Batteries register no "max_active_power" series.

Returns

A Dict mapping each PowerSimulations.TimeSeriesParameter type to its series name.

Updates a time-series parameter of a closed-loop run: PowerSimulations' own update reads the interval's series, then each component whose series is state-dependent (see is_state_dependent_input) gets the value closed_loop_input computes from its solved output at the previous interval. PowerSimulations.validate_template Method
julia
PSI.validate_template(model::PSI.DecisionModel{<:AbstractNEMDispatchProblem})

Checks that the system carries forecasts and that the availability of its devices and services is the one its NEMDE inputs were derived for, sets the Market Price Cap of model, then checks that the constraints the template excludes are constraints of the system, and runs check_template_against_sys and check_fcas_services. It throws when the template cannot model an available GenericConstraint it does not tolerate, deletes the per-name GenericConstraint models of the constraints the template leaves out (see template_skipped_constraints), runs check_dispatch_envelope over the dispatch intervals of the system, then the default template validation, which prunes device models with no available devices. The cap is the "market_price_cap_override" setting when set, else the one dated by the initial time, or by the system's forecast initial timestamp when the initial time is unset. The resolved cap is written to the "market_price_cap" setting on every call, so a rebuild at a later initial time re-dates it. The build replaces PSI's own balance slacks by AreaBalanceSlack only when the template holds an AEMSim formulation that adds them, and only on the build's copy of the template; a template of stock PSI formulations keeps its use_slacks.

Arguments

  • model: the NEM dispatch PSI.DecisionModel being built.

Returns

nothing. Throws ArgumentError from the checks, when the system has no forecasts or its availability changed after nem_system, or when no Market Price Cap is published for the date. The pruning changes the model's copy of the template, not the caller's template.

AustralianElectricityMarketsData.populate_legacy_archive Function
julia
populate_legacy_archive(db::AEMDB, table_name::Symbol, start_date::Date, end_date::Date; force_new::Bool=false)
populate_legacy_archive(db::AEMDB; tables=CONSTRAINT_DEFINITION_TABLES, start_date=Date(2009, 7, 1),
                        end_date=Date(2014, 12, 1), force_new::Bool=false)

Populate the Hive cache for months before 2015, when NEMWEB hosts only one monolithic MMSDM_<yyyy>_<mm>.zip per month (1.5 to 2.2 GB) instead of one ZIP per table. Each requested table's entry is read with HTTP range requests, so a month costs a few MB instead of the full archive, then written through the same pipeline as populate. Months already cached are skipped.

Use case: generic-constraint definitions. GENCONDATA and the SPD*CONSTRAINT term tables are effective-dated, and a monthly archive carries only the versions that became effective that month. A constraint last revised before 2015 (for example N_NIL_TE_B, effective 2012-07-04, or the Murraylink and Basslink *_ZERO constraints, effective 2013-08-21) is still invoked in DISPATCHCONSTRAINT today, but its definition appears only in a pre-2015 archive, so a cache populated from 2015-01 reports it as having no definition. The default tables are the four that define constraints.

Arguments

  • db::AEMDB: the cache connection.

  • table_name::Symbol / tables: tables to populate; each needs a PUBLIC_DVD_<table> entry in the archive.

  • start_date, end_date: first and last month to fetch, within 2009-07 to 2014-12.

  • force_new: re-fetch months already cached.

Example

julia
db = aem_connect()
populate_legacy_archive(db)                                   # constraint definitions, 2009-07 to 2014-12
populate_legacy_archive(db, :GENCONDATA, Date(2013, 8, 1), Date(2013, 8, 1))

AustralianElectricityMarketsCache.DataSource Type
julia
DataSource

Immutable description of one NEMWEB MMS table, cached as Hive-partitioned parquet under config.hive_location. Construction is pure — it does not touch the filesystem; _add_data creates path lazily on first write.

The filesystem ("file", "s3", "gs") is not stored separately — it's recovered from path's scheme via get_filesystem(::String), since path already encodes it (s3://..., gs://..., or a bare local path).

Fields

  • table_name::String: Name of the table

  • table_columns::Vector{String}: Columns to include

  • table_sort_by::Vector{String}: Columns to sort by within each output file (row-group locality; not an enforced uniqueness constraint)

  • partitions::Vector{String}: Partition columns

  • path::String: Path to parquet dataset (local path, or scheme://... URI for remote)

  • month_filter_column::Union{Nothing, String}: Column scoping rows to their archive month, or nothing

  • row_filter::Union{Nothing, Pair{String, String}}: column => value keeping only the rows whose raw column equals value, or nothing to keep every row

source
